units.name: reset_and_boot
units.description:
Cold entry: switch to native mode, set DP/DB to zero and put the stack at $01FF.
Initialize video and audio while blanked, clear frontend state and enter the attract/frontend dispatcher.
The final call selects the first track descriptor; race initialization follows physically.

units.name: initialize_selected_race
units.description:
Blank the display before replacing track-dependent video and world state.
Initialize four truck palette words, headings, movement accumulators and lap counters, then load terrain, route, graphics, HUD and objects.
Enable NMI and automatic joypad reads only after initialization. $052F lets the first prepared frame return instead of entering the race loop.
The unexplained $C8 per-truck counters are initialized here; their game meaning remains uncertain.

units.name: send_track_order_race_music
units.description:
Wait for the next NMI after the ready transition. If the race selector is nonzero, send command 1 with host music selector (track_order & 7)+6 in APU port 3.
The SPC decrements that selector, selecting songs 5..12. Native mode and DB/DP zero follow the inspected caller; SEP sets byte registers locally. Fall through to the existing race continuation.

units.name: run_race_frame
units.description:
Frame dispatcher: wait for vblank, collect input, then update movement, collisions, AI, sprites, track objects and HUD.
$88 selects the frame's rendering mode. A nonzero $052F returns after this prepared frame; ordinary play continues through the separate race-end checks.

units.name: return_prepared_race_frame
units.description: Return to the race initializer when its one-frame flag is set. This RTS shares the surrounding scheduler's caller stack.

units.name: test_human_race_mode
units.description: Separate human-controlled play from attract/demo handling using the active-controller mask. The adjacent completion branch now handles the winner transition.

units.name: dispatch_finished_race
units.description: While no winner is recorded, return to the race loop. Once winner_slot_plus_one is nonzero, run the result transition and re-enter race initialization.

units.name: repeat_until_race_winner
units.description: Keep dispatching race frames until the winner slot is nonzero. A winner transfers control to post-race handling.

units.name: finish_race_and_increment_order
units.description: Invoke the results/continuation flow, then increment the track-order slot. The following fragment wraps and resolves that slot.

units.name: wrap_track_order_and_reload
units.description:
Wrap the sequence index modulo 64, resolve its direction and track descriptor, then initialize the next race.
The preliminary low-nibble store is overwritten by select_track_descriptor; do not mistake it for the final track selection.

units.name: select_track_descriptor
units.description:
Read one of 64 track-order bytes using the sequence slot. Bit 7 becomes the reversed-direction flag; the low seven bits become the track ID.
Status is restored on return. The table supplies a fixed 16-track domain; reverse track 09 is absent from this natural order.

units.name: track_order_and_direction
units.description: 64 sequence bytes. Bit 7 selects reversed direction; bits 0..6 select the track descriptor. All sixteen track IDs occur, while reverse track 09 has no natural order slot.

units.name: send_race_sound_if_human
units.description:
Preserve the caller's 16-bit sound command while testing the low byte of the active-controller mask.
Write it to APU ports 2/3 only during human play; the alternate tail discards it during attract mode.

units.name: discard_attract_sound_command
units.description: Balance send_race_sound_if_human's saved accumulator without sending audio, then return.

units.name: poll_race_or_attract_start
units.description: Human play dispatches to its separate control handler; attract mode falls through to a Start-button test.

units.name: leave_attract_on_any_start
units.description:
Combine all four automatic joypad words and test Start ($1000).
On Start, discard the current return address, mark frontend reentry and jump into boot's frontend initialization. Otherwise return to the demo race.

units.name: check_other_truck_contacts
units.description:
For the current truck's word index in $49, scan the other three truck indices.
A squared coarse distance below $28 triggers contact resolution and starts a six-tick per-truck contact counter.
The distance helper uses Mode 7 multiplication for squared coordinate differences; axis differences at least $0A00 return the out-of-range sentinel $29.

units.name: measure_coarse_truck_distance
units.description:
Finish the absolute X difference and reject distant pairs, then square the reduced X and Y differences using Mode 7 multiplication.
Return their sum in 16-bit A. $54 holds the first square; the result is a coarse distance metric rather than a world-coordinate distance.

units.name: return_noncontact_distance
units.description: Return $29, safely above the contact cutoff $28, when either axis is too far apart.

units.name: classify_truck_contact_angles
units.description: Reduce signed truck separation through quantize_signed_vector_to_lookup_index and read a circular byte bearing from vector_direction_lookup. Save it as contact_normal_heading ($0529). Subtract the same normal from each truck heading, quantize both relative angles into four sectors and pack the pair into response-case nibbles. This consumer establishes heading arithmetic; it adds no natural read evidence for stored coordinate -8 cells.

units.name: reverse_contact_speeds
units.description: Negate the two contact speeds, retaining the other truck's original low byte in the accumulator high byte. Compare absolute magnitudes with $20 to select the high-speed or gentle collision response.

units.name: test_parallel_contact_sectors
units.description: Recognize packed sector pairs $00 and $22 as the shared speed-exchange response. Other combinations continue through later cases.

units.name: exchange_contact_motion
units.description:
Exchange current and other-truck movement values, then nudge the other heading by 16 angle units on alternating frame parity.
A speed difference of at least $20 requests impact audio; both paths continue to positional separation.

units.name: deflect_current_truck_contact
units.description:
Deflect the working truck after contact: if speed is below $60, add $20; then turn heading by eight, subtracting on odd animation frames and adding on even frames. This wraps the byte heading before continuing into terrain-tested pair separation.
Instruction boundaries require M8 only. State names assume DB00/DP0000 and the speed arithmetic description assumes decimal clear; these are semantic conditions, not observed arrival facts. No stack bytes are pushed here; the final jump shares the caller's return with the established separation tail.
The odd-frame store branches to the final transfer; it must skip the even-frame addition. Natural reachability remains unresolved.

units.name: deflect_oblique_truck_contacts
units.description:
Recognize the four odd-sector combinations and turn each heading by four angle units according to its side of the normal.
The remaining combinations transfer to the asymmetric response; accepted cases proceed to terrain-checked separation.

units.name: resolve_asymmetric_contact
units.description:
Choose an asymmetric heading/speed response from the packed sector bits. Some cases reduce the current movement accumulator by four.
Large movement values trigger impact audio before the shared positional correction. Two immediate loads are overwritten before use and are preserved faithfully.

units.name: separate_contact_pair_against_terrain
units.description:
Average the two truck positions, then place them on opposite sides using the contact-normal sine table and Mode 7 multiplication.
Accept each proposed position only when the terrain test returns carry clear. Current-truck correction goes through working coordinates; the other truck writes its position arrays.
The $0200 product scale controls the separation distance; this does not imply a physical world unit.

units.name: return_after_blocked_separation
units.description: Return without committing the other truck's proposed coordinates when terrain blocks them.

units.name: quantize_relative_heading_sector
units.description:
Map a wrapping 8-bit relative heading into four sectors centered on the cardinal directions.
The wraparound sector covers below $20 or at least $E0; remaining boundaries are $60 and $A0. Preserve Y and return the sector in A.

units.name: clear_wheel_state_and_select_route
units.description:
Clear three 16-byte wheel-state arrays. The internal route-loader entry masks the track ID to 16 slots and selects the normal/reversed pointer half.
The reverse-course branch adds $20 before the shared pointer store.

units.name: advance_route_pointer_reverse
units.description: The reverse-course route pointer skips $20 bytes before joining the common pointer store.

units.name: copy_selected_waypoint_stream
units.description:
Copy 16-bit route words into $079F until a word with high byte $FF. Its low byte supplies the route checkpoint count.
Initialize each truck's checkpoint index to one. The following internal start-grid entry selects heading data using track ID and direction.

units.name: offset_reversed_grid_heading
units.description: Rotate the start-grid heading by $20 for reversed courses; the following common tail stores it for each truck.

units.name: initialize_start_grid_heading
units.description:
Fetch the selected start heading and apply it to all four truck heading words.
The following path derives the grid displacement from that heading; reversed courses select $FC00.

units.name: reverse_grid_step
units.description: Use the negative fixed-point grid displacement $FC00 for the reversed starting order.

units.name: build_start_grid_positions
units.description:
Derive starting X/Y positions from the first route coordinate pair and a heading-dependent offset.
Build a two-by-two grid, copy positions to the truck arrays and sample terrain to initialize wheel and surface state.
The internal copy entry at $862C commits the eight prepared coordinate words.

units.name: commit_remaining_grid_x
units.description: Finish committing the prepared X coordinates for trucks 2, 3, 0 and 1. The adjacent setup has already staged these words in direct page.

units.name: alternate_start_grid_rows
units.description:
On odd track-order slots, exchange the prepared Y rows between paired trucks. Even slots return with the original grid.
The prepared X-coordinate commit joins this common tail.

units.name: track_start_heading_00
units.description: Byte heading for even source index 0, selected by track/reverse-track domain. The consumer indexes this byte at a two-byte stride within the bounded start-heading storage window; adjacent slot-internal semantics remain unresolved.

units.name: start_heading_stride_storage_window
units.description: The inspected bank-00 consumer masks the selector to 0..15, doubles it, adds $20 on the reverse path, and loads one M8 byte from $868B with DB=0. This bounds a 32-slot, two-byte-stride storage window at physical $068B..$06CB; the final selected byte is $06C9 and the next accepted code begins at $06CB. Interleaved-byte semantics and reachability remain unresolved.

units.name: poll_controls_and_check_routes
units.description:
Copy active human controller words, then visit enabled trucks to process route checkpoints.
Route high bytes $FE/$FD are special records; $FF wraps the checkpoint index. Ordinary checkpoints call the packed rectangle test.
The four-truck scan uses a shifted controller mask and a descending byte index; byte and word truck indices must not be interchanged.

units.name: wrap_route_checkpoint_index
units.description: A route terminator resets this truck's checkpoint index and rereads the start of its stream.

units.name: test_skippable_route_marker
units.description: Test the route word's $40 control bit before deciding whether to skip this checkpoint record.

units.name: skip_route_control_record
units.description: Advance to the next checkpoint and resume record interpretation without performing a rectangle test.

units.name: test_truck_checkpoint_rectangle
units.description:
Convert the byte truck slot to a word-array offset, then test its world position against the route rectangle.
Carry set rejects the checkpoint. On acceptance, advance its index; reaching index one marks a completed lap.

units.name: increment_truck_lap
units.description: Increment the truck's lap byte and update its lap display. The continuation compares this count with the race finish threshold.

units.name: declare_fifth_lap_winner
units.description: Only lap count five records this truck as winner. Store X+1 so zero continues to mean no winner, then join the checkpoint continuation.

units.name: test_route_checkpoint_limit
units.description: Compare the advanced checkpoint index with the route's terminator-supplied count. Below the count, continue scanning trucks; otherwise wrap the index.

units.name: reset_route_index_at_limit
units.description: Reset this truck's checkpoint index and resume the descending enabled-truck scan.

units.name: route_rectangle_and_controller_helpers
units.description:
The first RTS ends the route scan. Internal entry $8744 tests a packed checkpoint rectangle against truck X/Y and returns carry clear only inside both axes.
Each coordinate word stores its half-extent in low five bits and its center in the remaining coordinate bits. Unsigned range comparison handles both sides of the center.
Internal entry $8782 copies automatic joypad words into per-truck control words only for enabled controller slots.

units.name: copy_controller_two
units.description: Copy the second automatic controller word into truck 1's input slot.

units.name: test_controller_three_enabled
units.description: Shift the active-controller mask to decide whether controller three's word should be copied. The adjacent conditional copy writes that controller word into its truck input slot.

units.name: copy_controller_three
units.description: Copy the third automatic controller word into truck 2's input slot.

units.name: test_controller_four_enabled
units.description: Shift the active-controller mask to decide whether controller four's word should be copied. The adjacent conditional copy writes that controller word into its truck input slot.

units.name: copy_controller_four
units.description: Copy the fourth automatic controller word into truck 3's input slot.

units.name: return_after_controller_poll
units.description: Return after the four controller-enable tests; disabled slots retain their previous synthesized or inactive input.

units.name: clear_sprite_animation_cursors
units.description: Reset sixteen animation cursor bytes at $0519 before the track's sprite animation service starts.

units.name: animate_sixteen_sprite_slots
units.description:
Visit sixteen sprite slots, fetch paired tile/attribute values from the current animation cursor and write OAM shadow entries.
Advance animation only every fourth frame. $FE skips a slot update; $FF reaches the hide/reset tail.
The internal $87F6 entry converts a sprite slot to its four-byte OAM offset.

units.name: hide_finished_sprite_animation
units.description: Move this sprite's shadow Y to $F0, reset its animation cursor and continue the descending slot loop.

units.name: contact_animation_tile_stream
units.description: Selected contact-animation tile bytes. The shared cursor starts at 0/1/10/19 and advances once per four frames; $FE skips and $FF hides/resets. This selected 24-byte slice is followed by the independently supported seven-byte suffix; together the paired arrays have inferred capacity 31.

units.name: unselected_contact_animation_tiles
units.description: Six tile frames followed by $FF complete the contact animation at cursor 24. The paired tile and attribute origins $8804/$8823, synchronized terminators and following code at $8842 support an inferred 31-cell allocation. No natural writer selecting cursor 24 is known.

units.name: contact_animation_attribute_stream
units.description: Attribute bytes paired by cursor with the contact-animation tiles. $FE/$FF control handling and selected starts explain this 24-byte window; the paired seven-byte suffix completes an inferred 31-cell allocation.

units.name: unselected_contact_animation_attributes
units.description: Six OAM attribute bytes followed by $FF pair with the tile suffix at cursor 24. Both arrays share the same cursor and termination positions. The complete 31-cell allocation is inferred jointly; natural suffix selection remains unresolved.

units.name: quantize_signed_vector_to_lookup_index
units.description: Treat A low/high bytes as signed X/Y components. Halve both unsigned magnitudes together until each is at most seven, then restore four-bit signs and pack Y high/X low. Return a byte index into the complete stored bearing grid. Exhaustive scalar modeling over all 65,536 inputs confirms 225 outputs with components -7..7; neither component produces nibble $8, even for input -128. This read-domain result does not limit the stored coordinate grid (-8..7) or establish nonuse elsewhere. Preserve caller status; DP+$28/$29 and $54 are scratch. Internal $8885 bypasses AI when all trucks are human-controlled.

units.name: skip_human_ai_update
units.description: Bypass AI steering for a human-controlled truck and join the shared per-truck continuation.

units.name: steer_computer_trucks
units.description:
Visit truck slots whose bits are absent from the active human-controller mask. Set acceleration, select a route target with a per-truck lateral bias and convert its vector into a desired heading.
Call the steering helper, then update route progress. Internal entry $893E remembers the desired heading and handles the per-truck steering delay before applying it. The packed signed-coordinate bearing lookup returns a circular byte heading; adding one quarter turn ($40) converts it to the AI steering convention. Its quantizer reads only components -7..7; the complete stored grid also includes coordinate -8, whose natural reading remains unresolved.

units.name: clear_ai_route_bias
units.description: Clear this truck's route bias before continuing its steering update.

units.name: test_ai_steering_lock
units.description: A nonzero per-truck $0534 state prevents the ordinary steering adjustment. The adjacent lock tail decrements the lock and restores the saved index.

units.name: expire_steering_lock
units.description: Count down the steering lock, restore the caller's saved truck index and return.

units.name: turn_ai_toward_target
units.description:
Subtract the current heading from the desired wrapping angle. Inside the eight-unit deadband, leave heading unchanged; otherwise add or subtract the per-truck turn step in $2A.
The signed difference chooses the turn direction; saved status preserves that sign across the deadband test.

units.name: ai_truck_turn_steps
units.description: Four byte turn steps, indexed by descending truck ID 3..0.

units.name: tick_ai_route_timeout
units.description: Every other frame, decrement this truck's route timeout while preserving X. Expiry rewinds the checkpoint with route-end wrapping and resets the timeout.

units.name: rewind_ai_checkpoint
units.description: Step backwards through the AI route, wrapping a negative index to the route endpoint. Reset its waypoint timeout to 100 frames.

units.name: advance_ai_checkpoint_inside_rectangle
units.description:
The first tail restores X for the timeout helper. Internal entry $89AD ticks that timeout, then tests the truck against the next packed route rectangle.
On acceptance, update its route state and reload a timeout indexed by its parameter byte. Crossing the route boundary also increments the lap through a separate fragment.

units.name: restart_ai_route
units.description: Reset this truck's route index to the first checkpoint and return.

units.name: increment_ai_lap
units.description: Increment the computer truck's lap counter and refresh its lap display. The adjacent finish comparison is not included in this fragment.

units.name: record_ai_finish
units.description: Record X+1 as the winner only when the AI lap count reaches five.

units.name: select_next_ai_route_target
units.description:
The first RTS rejects an unaccepted checkpoint. Internal entry $8A1B clears the lateral bias and advances the route index.
Wide checkpoints permit a small random signed offset and start a 100-tick steering delay. $FD/$FE records redirect progress to an index stored in the next route byte.

units.name: randomize_ai_waypoint_advance
units.description: Use two low random bits to make route advancement occur on one of four outcomes; other outcomes branch to the shared continuation.

units.name: apply_ai_route_redirect
units.description: Read the route record's destination byte into the truck's checkpoint index and return.

units.name: advance_ai_checkpoint
units.description: Increment the truck's route checkpoint and return.

units.name: ai_parameter_waypoint_timeouts
units.description: Eight timeout bytes indexed by the AI parameter 0..7. Human speed upgrades are capped at 6; the parameter writers clamp their derived values to 0..7. Adjacent entries 8..15 remain unsupported.

units.name: build_truck_shadow_sprite
units.description:
Build the truck OAM shadow from projected position, palette attributes and average wheel height. The vertical adjustment also includes the projection term in $08.
Update this truck's packed OAM high-bit/size pair using its projected X high byte. $AA forces the large-sprite size bits while retaining the other trucks' X bits.

units.name: truck_oam_high_bit_mask_0
units.description: Selected even-index OAM high-bit mask byte for one truck. The indexed byte consumer does not establish the skipped odd cells.

units.name: truck_oam_high_bit_mask_1
units.description: Selected even-index OAM high-bit mask byte for one truck. The indexed byte consumer does not establish the skipped odd cells.

units.name: truck_oam_high_bit_mask_2
units.description: Selected even-index OAM high-bit mask byte for one truck. The indexed byte consumer does not establish the skipped odd cells.

units.name: truck_oam_high_bit_mask_3
units.description: Selected even-index OAM high-bit mask byte for one truck. The indexed byte consumer does not establish the skipped odd cells.

units.name: average_truck_surface_and_begin_suspension
units.description:
Average four terrain-target bytes into the truck's surface/height summary. Internal entry $8B24 integrates all sixteen wheel heights.
Clear per-truck contact markers, compare each wheel height with its target and select an upward impulse or a gravity update. Per-truck $062B modifies the upward step; its upgrade interpretation is tentative.

units.name: clamp_upward_wheel_step
units.description: Limit an upward wheel impulse to the step computed in $54; this belongs to suspension integration, despite the older generic OAM description.

units.name: integrate_wheel_vertical_motion
units.description:
Store the upward step and mark wheel/truck contact, or subtract $90 from the fractional vertical accumulator and borrow into the integer velocity.
Add that velocity to each wheel height. Internal entry $8B97 compares front/rear wheel sums to derive a signed speed correction for trucks with a contact marker.

units.name: apply_suspension_speed_and_pose
units.description:
Restore the sign of the wheel-slope correction and subtract it from truck speed unless signed overflow occurs.
Internal entry $8BDF visits four trucks to derive body tilt, choose a pose-table word and pack it for rendering. $8BFD rearranges fields of the selected pose word; $8C19 derives lateral tilt from opposite wheel sums.

units.name: clamp_longitudinal_pose_low
units.description: Clamp the longitudinal tilt selector to its lowest value before the common pose-index conversion.

units.name: limit_lateral_tilt_range
units.description: Check the positive lateral-tilt bound before quantizing it. The separate clamp tail selects $4F before quantization.

units.name: clamp_longitudinal_pose_high
units.description: Clamp the longitudinal tilt selector to $4F before the common pose-index conversion.

units.name: quantize_lateral_and_measure_longitudinal_tilt
units.description:
Divide the bounded lateral tilt by sixteen into $050F, then compute the front/back wheel-sum difference with a $28 bias.
The next fragments bound and quantize the longitudinal value independently.

units.name: clamp_lateral_pose_low
units.description: Clamp the lateral tilt selector to zero before the common pose-index conversion.

units.name: limit_longitudinal_tilt_range
units.description: Check the positive longitudinal-tilt bound. The separate clamp tail selects $4F.

units.name: clamp_lateral_pose_high
units.description: Clamp the lateral tilt selector to $4F before the common pose-index conversion.

units.name: select_truck_pose_from_tilts
units.description:
Quantize longitudinal tilt into $050D and heading into $050B. Internal entry $8C7C indexes a five-column tilt table with 5*longitudinal+lateral.
A nonzero tilt word halves the heading field before combining it with the pose word. The final packed pose is stored in $0509.

units.name: tilt_pose_word_grid
units.description: Five rows of five little-endian pose words. Index = 2*(5*longitudinal_tilt+lateral_tilt), with both tilt selectors clamped to 0..4. Heading bits are added later; this grid and the heading domain produce pose words 0..415.

units.name: update_four_trucks
units.description:
For each word-indexed truck, load controls, heading, position and speed into working variables. Sample wheel terrain, propose movement and resolve boundary/contact state.
$17/$18 select blocked-axis paths; only their mechanical use is established here. Wheel indices use four entries per truck, while $49 advances by two through position arrays.

units.name: restore_motion_before_blocked_response
units.description: Reload committed speed and position after a blocked proposal, then invoke projection, stuck-state and effect services. This path avoids committing the rejected coordinates.

units.name: commit_truck_motion_and_continue
units.description:
Update terrain-height summary, wheel response, projected coordinates and truck shadow sprite. Test truck contacts unless the collision cooldown is active, decrementing it otherwise.
Commit working speed, heading and world position, then advance to the next of four trucks.
Internal $8D86 computes Y/X displacement from heading-indexed signed vectors times speed using Mode 7 multiplication. Internal $8DD4 tracks repeated blocked motion and resets AI steering bias.

units.name: recover_stuck_ai_truck
units.description:
Reset the blocked-frame counter at sixteen. Human trucks retain normal control; computer trucks get a longer steering lock and movement value $81 to escape.
This is a bounded recovery mechanism; the exact signed speed convention remains uncertain.

units.name: track_airborne_contact_and_blocked_axes
units.description:
Restore registers for the blocked-motion helper. Internal entry $8E0F tracks transitions in the per-truck contact marker and starts an effect on recontact.
Inspect movement bit $80 before choosing the subsequent blocked-axis response; the separate flag-rotation tail exchanges the wheel-block byte pairs.

units.name: rotate_contact_block_flags
units.description: Rotate the two-byte wheel-block state into the companion flag pair for the contact transition calculation.

units.name: respond_to_blocked_x_axis
units.description:
If neither blocked-axis flag is set, clear the blocked-frame counter and return. One axis instead chooses a heading quadrant and rotates by minus four units.
A quadrant table decides whether to restore the X or Y working coordinate before applying the shared blocked response.

units.name: blocked_coordinate_by_heading_quadrant
units.description: Four low-byte selectors indexed by heading quadrant 0..3. The word consumer masks with $00FF, so its next-byte overread does not extend this structural table.

units.name: respond_to_blocked_y_axis
units.description: Rotate heading by plus four units within the 8-bit angle domain. A quadrant lookup selects the working coordinate to restore.

units.name: restore_blocked_coordinate_and_spawn_effect
units.description:
Restore the committed Y coordinate, or at internal $8EAE restore X, then run blocked-state and effect handling.
Internal $8EBC emits a short-lived effect only when the per-truck effect cooldown is zero and projected X fits one byte. Store its screen position and start a $18-tick cooldown.

units.name: initialize_track_countdown_display
units.description: Select a track-specific display word for the countdown/HUD shadow, install its attributes and clear animation counters. The separate track-eight setup places the countdown sprite pair at its alternate coordinates.

units.name: initialize_countdown_pair
units.description: Prepare two adjacent countdown sprites: tilewords $3180/$3182 and packed screen coordinates separated by sixteen pixels.

units.name: return_track_countdown_initialization
units.description: Restore the caller's processor status after track-specific display initialization.

units.name: track_countdown_oam_coordinates
units.description: Sixteen little-endian OAM coordinate words indexed by twice the selected track 0..15.

units.name: request_last_lap_banner
units.description:
At lap four or beyond, raise the banner counter to $1E if it is below $13. Preserve the byte truck index.
The race completion threshold is separately five; this helper starts the preceding display cue.

units.name: test_race_banner_counter
units.description: Preserve status and compare the banner counter with $13 before selecting its animation behavior.

units.name: suppress_banner_after_winner
units.description: A nonzero winner slot takes the banner service's return path rather than its normal update. Otherwise the adjacent pacing tail advances the state once every four frames.

units.name: pace_countdown_animation
units.description: Advance the countdown animation state only once every four animation frames.

units.name: update_banner_tile_and_secondary_sprite
units.description:
Use the banner counter to choose a tile/attribute word. Hide the secondary sprite while its subanimation counter is zero; counter $0F has a separate setup path.
The adjacent setup establishes the companion sprite offset and secondary state.

units.name: advance_countdown_secondary_sprite
units.description: Place the second countdown sprite four pixels after the first and select secondary state five.

units.name: animate_banner_secondary_sprite
units.description:
Decrement the subanimation every fourth frame, move the secondary shadow Y on odd frame parity and select its tile from a word table.
The final status-restoring return is a separate classified tail.

units.name: return_banner_service
units.description: Restore status and return after the banner shadow updates.

units.name: countdown_effect_tiles
units.description: Six little-endian OAM tile/attribute words indexed by the secondary countdown counter, which decreases from five through zero.

units.name: race_countdown_tiles
units.description: 35 little-endian OAM tile/attribute words. The startup, last-lap and postrace producers together establish selectors 0..34; this does not claim every selector was naturally observed.

units.name: halve_signed_truck_speed
units.description:
Take the magnitude of the low speed byte, halve it and restore its original sign. Preserve status.
This helper reduces motion without changing its signed direction.

units.name: upload_four_truck_pose_tiles
units.description:
For each truck, choose source bank one or two from the packed pose high bit. DMA two $40-byte strips, separated by $0200 in source and $0100 VRAM words in destination.
VRAM destinations begin at $6000 and advance $20 words per truck. Channel one uses mode 1 to the VRAM data ports.
This establishes the pose transfer mechanism; the complete source-selector domain remains a redirect question.

units.name: project_truck_to_screen
units.description: Preserve status, recover the truck word index and test track eight for a special projection adjustment. The special path tests a fixed world-Y band and surface threshold to choose sprite priority.

units.name: set_track_band_sprite_priority
units.description: For trucks inside the fixed world-Y band, compare the surface summary with $2E. Set the tileword priority bits on the elevated side; otherwise clear bit $1000. The world band and terrain threshold are exact; the visual obstruction they model remains uncertain.

units.name: store_truck_screen_coordinates
units.description: Store projected X minus $40 in the truck screen-X word, and projected Y plus $28 in its screen-Y byte. Restore caller status.

units.name: stage_hex_diagnostic_fields
units.description:
Initialize the direct-page output cursor to 2 and append hexadecimal glyph pairs for the high and low byte of each absolute field $04E9 and $04F1, leaving separator positions between fields.
With E=false, REP makes the field loads words and XBA presents high then low bytes to the preserving hex wrapper. E, DB and DP at entry remain unresolved: the native-word interpretation is conditional, and the encoded references do not prove WRAM identities.

units.name: initialize_sprite_arrays_and_pack_oam
units.description:
Initialize sixteen sprite IDs, clear X/attribute-related arrays and hide their screen Y values.
Internal entry $9155 visits the sorted sprite IDs and packs tile/attributes, X and Y into the OAM shadow at $0300. Collect X high bits and forced large-size bits into the OAM high table every eight sprites.
The packing scratch aliases change roles within this helper; their names must remain local or explicitly scratch.

units.name: sort_sprites_by_screen_y
units.description:
Stable insertion-sort sixteen sprite IDs by their screen-Y values in descending order.
Shift the ID array to insert an out-of-order sprite; equal Y values preserve their existing order. Screen coordinates and attributes remain in separate arrays, so only IDs move.

units.name: load_track_byte_parameters
units.description: Use the track ID as a byte-array index to load the terrain bank and first background pointer bank. The adjacent fragment loads the remaining parallel fields.

units.name: load_track_word_parameters
units.description:
Finish loading both background pointer banks and projection scales, then double the track index for word arrays.
Load X/Y projection offsets and the low words of both background pointers and the terrain source pointer. These fixed sixteen-slot fields establish table bounds independently of live track selection.

units.name: track_parameter_arrays
units.description:
Parallel sixteen-track fields: projection X/Y offset words, projection scale bytes, two background pointer low-word/bank arrays and terrain pointer bank/low-word arrays.
load_track_byte_parameters and load_track_word_parameters assemble them into direct-page working state; field symbols identify the exact subarray boundaries.

units.name: copy_track_terrain_and_upload_video
units.description:
Internal $932A copies exactly $16B1 terrain bytes through the 24-bit pointer at $23 into WRAM $7F0000.
Internal $933F loads track parameters, copies terrain and uses a three-byte pointer to DMA $8000 graphics bytes into VRAM.
Upload the shared $200-byte palette, clear three background maps, then copy $600 bytes into each of two maps. The second map forces tile attribute bit $2000.
HDMA is disabled before transfer. Preserve caller status at both public entries.

units.name: track_graphics_source_pointers
units.description: Sixteen little-endian 24-bit CPU source pointers, indexed by 3*trackID. Each consumer requests an $8000-byte graphics DMA; CPU bank wrapping must be interpreted on the bus.

units.name: decode_controller_direction_words
units.description:
Convert the controller word's upper-byte low nibble to two signed 16-bit direction components. Multiply the 0..15 selector by two, then store paired table words at DP+$11 and DP+$13.
Entry requires native E=0 and an ordinary same-bank JSR return. REP20 and SEP10 establish body widths independently of incoming M/X. DB/DP do not affect decoding; controller/table/state names assume DB00/DP0000, inferred separately from the byte helper and paired table layout.
PHP/PLP restores P; A and X are scratch. Y low, DB and DP are unchanged, but SEP10 clears Y high when entering with native X16. Restoring X width cannot recover discarded index high bytes. Natural entry and actual incoming bank/status are unresolved.

units.name: menu_direction_first_00
units.description: Selected direction byte at even index 0. The M8 helper consumes this low byte; the paired high byte is now classified for the conditional native helper under an inferred DB00 table association.

units.name: controller_direction_word_high_1439
units.description:
High byte of signed direction component 0 in the first sixteen-word table. Paired with the preceding low byte, this extends the existing M8 table use to the conditional native word helper.
The DB00 table association is a static inference from bounded word indexing, paired bases and the independent byte consumer; no helper execution or natural entry is claimed.

units.name: update_acceleration_from_upgrades
units.description:
Run steering and nitro processing before normal acceleration. Accumulate a fractional acceleration term indexed by the per-truck upgrade, retaining its low byte and using its high byte as this frame's speed step.
Acceleration requires the B input bit and the per-truck contact marker. Choose a speed-limit table offset from boost state and human/AI control. The negative-speed path adds its fractional correction before the common store.

units.name: add_acceleration_fraction
units.description: Add the accumulated fractional speed correction and join the common speed update.

units.name: limit_acceleration_and_apply_drag
units.description:
Compare speed with the selected limit, add the fractional carry step below the limit and reject signed overflow.
At or beyond the limit, reduce speed on alternating frames. The no-acceleration entry $94F4 applies drag toward zero; its separate negative-speed tail increments toward zero.

units.name: drag_negative_speed_toward_zero
units.description: Increase a negative working speed toward zero, restore the caller's status and return.

units.name: decrement_positive_speed_for_drag
units.description: Reduce positive speed by one and restore the acceleration caller's status. The negative-speed counterpart increments toward zero.

units.name: upgrade_speed_limits
units.description: Nine speed-limit bytes: human upgrade 0..6, bounded AI parameter up to 7 and the special zero-upgrade AI selector 8. These are lookup values, not physical speed units.

units.name: upgrade_acceleration_fraction_steps
units.description: Seven little-endian fractional acceleration steps for the supported upgrade domain 0..6. The carry into the integral speed update supplies the effective acceleration.

units.name: consume_nitro_on_press_edge
units.description:
Skip nitro during the prepared initialization frame. Rotate the Y-button state through a per-truck history byte and act only on a new press.
If BCD nitro stock is nonzero, subtract one in decimal mode, force movement to $7C, start the boost sprite when projected X fits a byte and request boost audio.
Internal $9575 accumulates a steering rate selected by the tire/steering upgrade; only on accumulator carry do direction bits turn the heading by eight units.

units.name: step_pose_angle_left
units.description: Decrease the working pose angle by four and wrap it to eight bits.

units.name: test_left_steering_input
units.description: Test the alternate left-direction bit after the preceding direction path. Its turn body begins at the following fragment.

units.name: turn_heading_positive_eight
units.description: Add eight angle units and wrap heading to eight bits. This is a steering operation; the prior generic sprite-transfer label was misleading.

units.name: test_alternate_steering_input
units.description: Test the remaining direction bit before its separate heading update. The corresponding update adds four and wraps the heading to eight bits.

units.name: step_pose_angle_right
units.description: Increase the working pose angle by four and wrap it to eight bits.

units.name: return_steering_update
units.description: Return after the rate-limited steering checks.

units.name: heading_x_vector_words
units.description: 32 signed little-endian fixed-point X vector words, selected by (heading>>3)*2. Movement multiplies this vector by speed using the Mode 7 arithmetic registers.

units.name: heading_y_vector_words
units.description: 32 signed little-endian fixed-point Y vector words paired with heading_x_vector_words. Equal indexing preserves direction; physical world units remain uncertain.

units.name: upgrade_steering_rates
units.description: Seven steering-rate bytes indexed by the supported upgrade domain 0..6.

units.name: sample_wheels_and_project_world_position
units.description:
Sample all four wheel positions against terrain. Carry clear stores the returned height; carry set records the blocking direction plus one in the wheel collision flags.
Recover the truck's average surface/height byte after the scan. Internal $969A applies the track's projection scales and offsets using Mode 7 multiplication, forming projected X in $84 and an intermediate projected Y.
World coordinates and intermediate products are fixed-point values; their exact real-world units are not established.

units.name: finish_projection_and_classify_terrain
units.description:
Finish projected Y using the surface-height contribution and $2C00 baseline, then return screen Y in $86.
Internal $974F loads a terrain neighborhood, selects a packed quadrant from relative X/Y and tests its blocking bits. Clear quadrants proceed to height interpolation; blocked quadrants select directional return tails.
$65 receives one shifted terrain control bit. Its later game meaning remains uncertain.

units.name: select_diagonal_terrain_block_direction
units.description: Recognize masked neighborhood patterns $0A/$88/$A0, directing each to its corresponding diagonal blocking return. Other patterns take the shared fallback.

units.name: skip_diagonal_block_load
units.description: Skip the embedded $A0 load through BIT's operand bytes, retaining the caller's A. Alternate entries load $A0/$E0/$20/$60 before restoring status and returning carry set. The trailing neighborhood entry reads another terrain row. Internal LDA entries share these bytes; they are not duplicate storage.

units.name: inspect_adjacent_terrain_blocks
units.description:
Probe the four neighboring packed terrain-control bytes for an opening when the local cell is fully blocked.
If a neighbor is open, use a cardinal blocking code; otherwise match neighboring diagonal patterns to the diagonal return entries. These reads can address the preceding row via $7EFFFF aliases and must retain their encoded long addresses.

units.name: test_cardinal_neighbor_blocks
units.description: Inspect the two neighboring terrain bit pairs for the cardinal blocked-edge patterns. Matching patterns enter shared directional return tails; otherwise seed direction $08 and continue through the BIT skip prefix.

units.name: skip_cardinal_block_load
units.description: Skip the embedded $C0 load through BIT's operand bytes. Internal LDA entries choose $C0/$00/$40/$80; all converge on status restore and carry-set return. The prefix retains A on the skip path.

units.name: normalize_terrain_triangle_and_interpolate
units.description:
Reflect negative fractional X/Y to nonnegative coordinates while exchanging corner heights to keep the same geometric patch.
Choose an interpolation triangle by comparing the reflected fractions. Combine signed corner-height slopes with the two fractions using Mode 7 products and a common base.
Track eight has a separate interpolation finish; ordinary terrain returns the interpolated height with carry clear.

units.name: finish_horizontal_terrain_probe
units.description: Move the interpolated component into the low accumulator byte, subtract $20 and restore caller status. Carry clear reports a height result rather than a blocking direction.

units.name: return_height_or_interpolate_other_triangle
units.description:
Return the first triangle height from the accumulator high byte with carry clear. Internal $989A performs the alternate triangle's corner-slope products.
Both formulas share the normalized coordinates and base term. The track-eight adjustment branch remains outside this classified fragment.

units.name: finish_vertical_terrain_probe
units.description: Move the vertical interpolation component into the low byte, subtract $20 and restore caller status. Carry clear identifies the nonblocking result.

units.name: return_height_and_load_terrain_neighborhood
units.description:
Return the alternate height with carry clear. Internal $98EB computes a terrain-cell index from high coordinate bytes using a row-offset table and three-byte cell stride.
Load five neighboring heights and the packed control byte into direct-page scratch. Internal $992A computes a wheel probe position from the truck heading, wheel-specific angular offset and signed sine table.
The wheel probe outputs are world coordinates at $43/$45; they feed the terrain classifier.

units.name: wheel_heading_phase_offsets
units.description: Four byte phase offsets added modulo 256 to the heading before signed sine lookup, one per wheel.

units.name: initialize_race_oam_shadow
units.description:
Initialize 128 OAM shadow entries as hidden Y=$F0 with default attributes. Configure color math and sub-screen layers, then initialize the 32-byte OAM high table.
Two high-table overrides establish initial size/X-bit state for special sprites. Preserve status.

units.name: next_pseudorandom_byte
units.description:
Mix the five-byte direct-page state using shifts, rotates and XOR, and return the new first byte.
Preserve X and processor status around the state transformation. The final load uses the restored accumulator width; callers requiring a byte must establish it. No statistical randomness quality is claimed.

units.name: initialize_sprite_dma
units.description: Configure DMA channel zero for byte transfers to OAM data, bank zero, then select OBJ tile base/size. Source and length are installed by the upload helper.

units.name: upload_oam_shadow
units.description: Reset the OAM address and DMA $220 bytes from bank-zero RAM $0200, including the 32-byte high table. Preserve caller status; channel zero must already target OAM.

units.name: fade_out_fade_in_and_wait_frame
units.description:
Fade-out entry waits for a frame, resets the animation counter and decreases brightness over sixteen ticks, ending in forced blank.
Internal $9A42 installs the enabled-layer mask and fades in over thirty-two ticks using half the animation counter.
Internal $9A64 waits until the independent NMI frame counter changes. NMI must be enabled for these busy waits to complete.

units.name: wait_x_frame_boundaries_preserving_status
units.description:
Save status, wait for NMI, decrement X and repeat until zero, then restore status. Nonzero entry X gives that many frame boundaries; zero wraps through the current index width.
Entry E/DB/DP and X width remain caller-specific and unresolved. The fixed-length loop is established independently of natural reachability; this is not a newly observed gameplay route.

units.name: load_shared_sprite_palette_and_tiles
units.description:
Copy $100 palette bytes from $04EB00 into the upper half of CGRAM. Internal $9A9C disables HDMA and installs two shared sprite graphics transfers.
The first requests $3C00 bytes from CPU $02D000; DMA crosses its sixteen-bit source boundary, so only the ROM-backed prefix is classified. The second copies $1040 bytes from $04DAC0.
VRAM destinations are $6200 and $77E0 words; preserve status.

units.name: offset_grid_8x8
units.description: Each 16-bit little-endian cell equals (row * $0400) + (column * $0040), for rows and columns 0..7. This establishes the stored offset grid and its exact 128-byte bounds; its consumer and intended purpose are unknown.

units.name: load_font_and_clear_bg
units.description: Upload exactly $800 font bytes from $08DA20 to VRAM word $5000, then clear the background map at $4800. Preserve status; the clear helper has its documented inclusive count.

units.name: append_hex_byte_preserving_registers
units.description:
Preserve A, X and status at their incoming widths, set byte accumulator/index widths, and append the two hexadecimal glyphs for A low. Restore status before restoring registers.
E/DB/DP at entry remain unresolved. Under native entry with X16, SEP clears X high and the saved full X is restored. Storage operands in the callee remain relative to the unknown direct page.

units.name: append_hex_byte_glyphs
units.description:
With M8/X8, retain the input byte while appending its high nibble, then append its low nibble through the shared internal helper.
The helper maps nibble 0..15 to glyph 1..16 and advances the byte cursor at DP+$88, writing DP+$89+X. E/DB/DP and natural entry remain unresolved; these symbolic offsets are not absolute RAM assertions.

units.name: service_nmi_video_and_input
units.description:
Save 16-bit A/X/Y and clear decimal mode. When the video-update inhibit byte is zero, upload OAM and current truck pose graphics.
Always advance frame counters and send the incrementing audio heartbeat through APU port zero. Wait for automatic controller polling to finish before restoring registers and RTI.
Status comes from the hardware interrupt stack; the handler does not assume caller M/X widths.

units.name: fill_vram_with_caller_word
units.description: Preserve status and share the clear helper's body, retaining the caller's fill word in A and destination VRAM word in X.

units.name: clear_vram_and_reset_ppu
units.description:
Clear entry supplies zero before the common fill body at $9C13. It writes $401 words because the loop includes X=$0400 through zero; callers and port code must retain that inclusive endpoint.
Internal $9C2A forces blank and resets PPU object/background/window/color registers. Scroll registers are written twice to clear both latches.
These are separate callable entries within one classified physical run.

units.name: vector_heading_cells_00
units.description: Complete stored signed-nibble bearing grid: ROM $001CC7..$001DC7, encoded CPU origin $009CC7 in bank $00. Index = ((y & 15) << 4) | (x & 15), with both coordinates signed -8..7. Each byte is a circular heading (256 units per turn); collision code subtracts it from truck headings, while AI adds $40 before steering. All 255 nonzero vectors agree within one circular heading unit with -atan2(y,x)*128/pi; the zero vector retains its existing $FF byte without a defined geometric bearing. This describes the finite stored values, not an exact generator or rounding rule. The inferred 256-byte extent joins the decoded coordinate/heading type and 225 prior typed cells with the full nonlinear grid and independent sine-source origin $009DC7. There is no encoded allocation count. The established magnitude-reduction producer yields only -7..7 in each component (225 indices, confirmed over all 65,536 byte pairs). Stored coordinate -8 capacity is distinct from that read domain; natural nibble-$8 reads remain unresolved. No nonuse, dead-data or new execution claim follows.

units.name: vector_heading_x_minus8_y_0
units.description: Bearing-grid indices $08..$08; signed (x,y) from (-8, 0) through (-8, 0). Same byte-heading format and stored extent as vector_heading_cells_00; natural read domain remains separate. These coordinate -8 cells complete the inferred stored grid; the established quantizer does not produce them.

units.name: heading_signed_sine
units.description: 256 signed byte samples indexed by heading plus wheel phase modulo 256. Quarter-turn phase aliases use the same byte arithmetic; numerical scale remains a game-specific projection factor.

units.name: track_cgram_source_prefix
units.description:
The unknown complement at the start of the 512-byte CPU $009EC7 transfer window. The byte copy sends this range to CGRAM, but the complete read window also overlaps row-offset data and executable code at $00A037..$00A0C7.
This is a bounded transfer-source role, not a disjoint 512-byte palette allocation or proof that code bytes are color-format records.

units.name: initialize_frontend_and_attract
units.description:
Send frontend audio command, reset display state and enable NMI/controller polling. Check a five-byte RAM signature to decide whether the licensed splash is needed.
Initialize persistent frontend records and save the stack for nonlocal Start reentry. Clear upgrades and stock, then choose one of four attract track-order slots.
$D2 bypasses the attract setup after Start; attract mode has no active human controller bits and gives its trucks BCD nitro stock $99.

units.name: attract_track_order_slots
units.description: Four attract sequence slots. The consumer masks its slot index with3; each byte selects a track-order position.

units.name: resume_frontend_from_start
units.description:
Restore the saved frontend stack, initialize driver selection and its display, and restart attract initialization if nobody joined.
Otherwise combine the two player-choice bytes into the active truck/controller mask; the following AI setup assigns initial nitro to nonhuman slots.

units.name: give_ai_initial_nitro
units.description: Visit all four truck slots with a shifting human mask. Nonhuman trucks receive BCD $15 nitro; reset the track-order slot after initialization.

units.name: inhibit_race_video_and_clear_window
units.description: Increment the NMI video-update inhibit byte before clearing window masks. The next block forces display blank before returning.

units.name: blank_display_after_attract_setup
units.description: Finish attract setup by forcing display blank; return with an eight-bit accumulator.

units.name: show_licensed_splash
units.description:
Force blank, enable the first background layer and load frontend graphics. Use the ten-word rectangle descriptor to draw the licensed splash map, then fade in.
The source pointer bank is five; width/height and palette substitutions come from the descriptor.

units.name: set_frontend_wait_140
units.description: Initialize the frontend wait timer to 140 before entering its common timed sequence.

units.name: wait_and_replace_startup_splashes
units.description:
Wait a frame at a time for Start or timeout, fade out, replace the licensed map with the software splash and fade in.
After another $6E-tick wait, install the five-byte initialized-RAM signature and fade out. Start can unwind to the saved frontend stack through the poll helper.

units.name: frontend_initialization_signature_bytes
units.description: Five bytes compared and copied by frontend RAM initialization. The descending index 4..0 fixes the signature extent; retain literal values without assigning text meaning.

units.name: licensed_splash_rectangle_descriptor
units.description:
Ten little-endian words for draw_remapped_tile_rectangle: width/flags, height and eight palette substitutions.
Width=18, height=25; width bit 15 permits palette remapping. The caller supplies the separate source pointer and VRAM destination.

units.name: software_splash_rectangle_descriptor
units.description:
Ten little-endian words for draw_remapped_tile_rectangle: width/flags, height and eight palette substitutions.
Width=23, height=17; width bit 15 permits palette remapping. The caller supplies the separate source pointer and VRAM destination.

units.name: load_frontend_graphics_and_prepare_attract_panel
units.description:
Inhibit race uploads and disable HDMA, clear the frontend map and copy two bounded graphics spans to VRAM. Initialize palette zero, then upload $E0 palette bytes.
Internal $A248 blanks the screen, clears per-truck upgrades/stock, loads the attract display, enables its layers and initializes the window/object presentation before its frame loop.

units.name: draw_attract_overlay_each_frame
units.description: Lower brightness while updating the frontend overlay, restore full brightness and poll Start/timeout. Continue the preceding frame loop while its result is nonnegative.

units.name: allow_window_start_abort
units.description: Enable the window transition's Start-abort path, initialize the frontend transition and join its input/render setup before returning.

units.name: initialize_frontend_window_motion
units.description: Initialize window center/extent and three control bytes, then select 16-bit accumulator mode. The following block uses the selected word width to start the window animation.

units.name: animate_scrolling_window
units.description:
Clear window extent, start a100-frame timer and show the screen. Each frame grows extent by max(extent/16,1), moves X left and bounces Y between64and160 with a signed step.
BG1 scroll is the negative of each center plus its display offset. Optional Start exits immediately; otherwise stop after the extent high byte reaches4, then disable the window.

units.name: expand_and_bounce_frontend_window
units.description:
Initialize a frontend window transition with extent zero, center motion -2 and three $22 control bytes. Install the window setup and update once per frame.
When enabled, Start can abort through a later exit. The remaining fragment grows the extent and oscillates its center.

units.name: allow_start_to_abort_window
units.description: Combine the first two controller high bytes and test Start. A press exits the window transition through its separate cleanup path.

units.name: grow_window_extent_and_move_center
units.description:
Increase the fixed-point extent by max(extent/16,1), decrease the vertical parameter and move the horizontal center by its signed velocity.
Reverse horizontal motion at centers $40 and $B0; the fixed-point high byte later bounds the duration.

units.name: reverse_window_horizontal_velocity
units.description: Negate the signed center velocity when a transition boundary is reached.

units.name: test_window_expansion_limit
units.description: Repeat the frame update while the extent high byte is below four. The transition duration depends on the accelerating extent.

units.name: blank_and_cleanup_window
units.description: Force blank, clear all window masks and return to the caller.

units.name: begin_contracting_window
units.description:
Initialize a centered window with extent $0400 and install its geometry. Wait one frame per update and optionally permit a Start abort.
The following supported path contracts the extent until its high byte becomes negative.

units.name: test_first_two_start_buttons
units.description: Combine the first two controller high bytes and test Start. A press selects the frontend exit path.

units.name: contract_window_until_closed
units.description:
Update the window geometry, then subtract max(extent/16,1) each frame. Continue while the high byte is nonnegative.
Force blank and clear masks when closed. The signed underflow is the exit condition rather than an exact-zero test.

units.name: blank_before_frontend_upload
units.description: Force blank and call the frontend graphics setup wrapper. Establish index and accumulator widths before the unresolved continuation.

units.name: show_scrolling_highscores
units.description:
Draw the frontend rectangle and ten-row high-score display, then fade in at BG3 scroll$0118.
Wait up to500frames or Start while increasing scroll toward$01D6. The register receives the pre-increment value, so the RAM increment appears on the following frame.
Enable Start abort for the closing-window helper and poll once more before returning.

units.name: rank_trucks_by_race_progress
units.description:
Create four candidate lap counters, then repeatedly select the greatest lap/checkpoint progress into the ranking array.
For equal lap and checkpoint indices, compare distance to the next route coordinate. A route low-five-bit extent of one chooses X distance; otherwise use Y.
Use absolute differences, mark each chosen candidate $FF and continue until all four ranks are filled. Preserve status.

units.name: break_ranking_tie_with_y_distance
units.description: Compare both tied trucks' absolute Y distance to the next waypoint. Branch to retain or replace the current best candidate.

units.name: store_next_ranked_truck
units.description:
Restore the candidate index after tie testing, update the best lap/checkpoint values when needed and finish scanning candidates.
Write the best truck ID to the next rank, mark it used and repeat for all four ranks.

units.name: truck_participation_bits
units.description: Four bit masks indexed by the ranked truck IDs 0..3, used against the active-human mask.

units.name: derive_ai_parameters_from_human_upgrades
units.description:
Scan active human trucks for maximum and minimum upgrade values. Inactive trucks get suspension parameter six.
Set four AI parameter bytes from the maximum minus one, with a separate minimum-derived value and later per-slot adjustment. These mechanics suggest difficulty balancing; the exact game interpretation remains tentative.

units.name: clear_ranking_candidate
units.description: Use zero for this ranking candidate in the shared ranking store.

units.name: store_minimum_ai_parameter
units.description: Store the minimum-derived parameter in one truck slot and test the fourth truck's human-control bit before a separate override.

units.name: advance_rank_scan_index
units.description: Continue backwards through the candidate slots while the index remains nonnegative.

units.name: raise_ai_parameter_with_cap
units.description: Compute maximum upgrade plus two and compare with seven before a separate clamp. The cap branch supplies seven to the shared store.

units.name: set_attract_ai_parameter
units.description: Use parameter seven for the attract-mode AI adjustment.

units.name: return_after_ai_parameter_setup
units.description: Store the selected per-truck parameter and restore the setup caller's status.

units.name: adjust_ai_state_using_race_rank
units.description:
Preserve X/Y and rank the trucks, then find the current truck's position while counting preceding computer-controlled slots.
Subtract that count to obtain a human-relative rank. A random byte and rank-indexed thresholds select later adjustment paths; the adjacent adjustment bodies compare the upgrade with its target and apply the random threshold.

units.name: count_preceding_computer_truck
units.description: Increment the ranking helper's scratch count when a preceding ranked truck is computer-controlled.

units.name: test_rank_based_random_adjustment
units.description:
Finish finding the current rank, subtract preceding computer trucks and compare a pseudorandom byte against a rank-indexed threshold.
The selected adjustment body follows separately and may lower a nonzero AI speed upgrade.

units.name: adjust_ai_speed_upgrade
units.description: Compare each AI speed upgrade against its target parameter. When equal, use lap and rank-dependent random thresholds to force a temporary all-button controller word; otherwise increase a below-target upgrade through the shared adjustment path. Human/AI selection and index scaling come from the surrounding rank-balancing routine.

units.name: test_second_rank_adjustment_threshold
units.description: Compare the same selection byte against the second rank-indexed threshold before choosing a later adjustment.

units.name: decrease_ai_speed_upgrade
units.description: Reduce a nonzero AI speed upgrade by one, retaining zero as the lower bound.

units.name: return_rank_adjustment_helper
units.description: Restore 16-bit Y/X and caller status for the rank-based adjustment helper.

units.name: ai_parameter_random_threshold_prefix
units.description: First five bytes of the eight-byte AI parameter threshold window at CPU $A687. The consumer reaches this lookup only when current speed equals the bounded AI parameter 0..7. The last three bytes share the following rank threshold role.

units.name: ai_and_human_rank_random_thresholds
units.description: Three shared threshold bytes: tail of the AI parameter lookup at $A687 and prefix of the human-relative-rank window at $A68C. These are one physical role with two consumers; thresholds control RNG comparisons, not probabilities with established units.

units.name: human_rank_random_threshold_tail
units.description: Remaining supported bytes of the human-relative-rank threshold windows rooted at $A68C and $A690. The ranker counts preceding AI trucks to derive human-relative position 0..3; the windows overlap, so do not treat this slice as an independent record.

units.name: begin_postrace_presentation
units.description:
Update the HUD and wait a frame. Every eighth sequence slot, increment a capped progression byte.
Disable HDMA and inhibit race uploads before configuring a channel-one graphics transfer from bank seven. The next fragment supplies the map destination, source and length before entering countdown setup.

units.name: transfer_race_entry_map
units.description: Finish DMA channel 1 setup for a $0DC0-byte map transfer to VRAM $55C8. Enable the transfer, release race-video inhibition and enter the countdown/window setup.

units.name: normalize_postrace_checkpoint_indices
units.description: Visit four checkpoint indices and compare each with the route count. The adjoining correction subtracts the route count before storing the wrapped checkpoint.

units.name: wrap_finished_checkpoint
units.description: Subtract the route checkpoint count from this truck's index to wrap it into the next lap.

units.name: rank_finished_race_and_fade_out
units.description: Continue the descending checkpoint scan, rank the trucks and fade out the race display.

units.name: show_postrace_awards
units.description:
Inhibit race video updates, clear color math and prepare the awards/podium display while blank.
Initialize its text/accounting services, request audio command $0401 and fade in. Set a $190-frame display timeout for the following awards loop.

units.name: wait_awards_frame_and_test_pending_count
units.description: Wait one frame and test the low byte of the pending awards/accounting count at $0728. Nonzero counts take the timed record-save/blink path before input polling.

units.name: commit_or_flash_track_record
units.description: At timer 250, save the race time and the winner's three-byte name into this track's record, then refresh the record display. Later frames blink its tile row according to animation bit $10; earlier frames continue normal record rendering.

units.name: dismiss_awards_on_input_or_timeout
units.description: Any bit in the first two joypad words dismisses the awards screen. Otherwise decrement its 16-bit timer and repeat until it becomes negative.

units.name: settle_awards_and_test_losing_human
units.description:
Disable transition input, contract the awards window and visit four pending award bytes, invoking the money helper for each nonzero entry.
Then test whether the last-ranked truck is human-controlled before entering loss/continuation handling.

units.name: jump_race_end_continuation
units.description: Join the common race-end continuation without adding another return frame.

units.name: count_active_humans_for_continue
units.description:
Count active controller bits, preserve the count and losing truck index across loss-display helpers, then distinguish one-human continuation from multiplayer behavior.
For a single human, decrement the continuation/progression byte before the loss penalty; the underflow branch clears continuation state and explicitly unwinds to frontend entry.

units.name: restart_after_continue_loss
units.description: Clear continuation progress, update the human-player mask and frontend state, discard the saved return frames and jump to the initial frontend entry. The explicit stack unwind is part of this path's contract.

units.name: penalize_losing_truck_upgrades
units.description: Reduce the losing truck's four upgrade bytes by two, clamping each at zero. Clear its six-byte money/accounting record, mark its continuation state and show the loss screen.

units.name: test_continue_choice
units.description: Test the saved loss-screen choice before returning to player setup; the alternate branch updates the last-ranked truck participation mask.

units.name: remove_last_ranked_human
units.description: Select the last-ranked truck and update its participation mask. With no humans remaining, branch into the common no-player path.

units.name: resume_shop_after_continue
units.description: Reenter the player/shop frontend after continuation is accepted.

units.name: settle_inactive_truck_stock_and_return
units.description: Run the inactive-truck money-to-stock helper, restore the results caller's status and return.

units.name: toggle_human_participation
units.description: Toggle the selected truck's participation bit, split the resulting mask into two frontend page masks and clear continuation progress. Preserve the caller's processor status.

units.name: load_wipeout_graphics
units.description:
Inhibit race uploads and disable HDMA, clear the display map and upload two graphics spans and a $C0-byte palette.
The losing truck index selects an optional palette adjustment; the separate selected palette path copies its colors to CGRAM.

units.name: load_result_palette
units.description: Select a palette offset from the result selector and copy $60 bytes from CPU bank $08 into CGRAM starting at color $29.

units.name: draw_wipeout_background
units.description:
Draw the loss map from bank eight using its rectangle descriptor, upload shared text/font resources and clear the text background.
Request loss audio command $1001 and distinguish attract mode from human continuation.

units.name: jump_continue_prompt_setup
units.description: Enter the shared continue-prompt display setup.

units.name: show_continue_prompt_and_cursor
units.description:
Draw the continuation prompt text and initialize paired nine-sprite cursor tiles. Reset sprite state, install the cursor geometry and fade in with choice zero.
The cursor uses separate OAM copies for the prompt alternatives; the main loop polls the losing truck's controller.

units.name: poll_continue_controller
units.description: Wait for a frame, select the losing truck's controller high byte and test B for acceptance. The adjoining left/right fragments toggle the choice and reposition its cursor.

units.name: select_continue_left
units.description: Move a nonzero continue choice to the left option and seed its cursor X coordinate with $24.

units.name: test_continue_right_input
units.description: Test the right direction bit; without it repeat the continuation input loop. The adjoining choice-update body selects the right option and redraws its cursor.

units.name: select_continue_right
units.description: Move the zero continue choice to the right option, place its cursor at $A8 and redraw the composite cursor before returning to the prompt loop.

units.name: dismiss_continue_prompt
units.description: Upload the final display shadow, contract the prompt window and restore the loss-screen caller's status.

units.name: draw_continue_prompt
units.description: Draw the continue rectangle at VRAM $4B0B, wait for a frame, enable the intended layers and enter the prompt's common timing/input code.

units.name: wait_frontend_controller_or_timeout
units.description:
Wait through at most301frame boundaries; test the high controller bytes from all four ports. A nonzero input follows the existing frontend response path.
The signed X countdown expiry rejoins the earlier timeout path; this tail relies on the caller-specific index-width contract.

units.name: paired_text_glyphs_2a32
units.description: Glyph-index stream through its first $FF terminator, selected by an explicit source pointer passed to the paired-tile text consumer. Literal glyph codes retain the local font encoding; no unsupported text identity is assigned.

units.name: result_palette_offsets
units.description: Three little-endian source offsets for nonzero ranked-truck values, indexed by twice rank-minus-one. Each selects a 96-byte palette replacement.

units.name: paired_text_glyphs_2a43
units.description: Glyph-index stream through its first $FF terminator, selected by an explicit source pointer passed to the paired-tile text consumer. Literal glyph codes retain the local font encoding; no unsupported text identity is assigned.

units.name: continue_picture_rectangle
units.description:
Ten little-endian words for draw_remapped_tile_rectangle: width/flags, height and eight palette substitutions.
Width=32, height=23; width bit 15 permits palette remapping. The caller supplies the separate source pointer and VRAM destination.

units.name: result_truck_participation_bits
units.description: Four masks indexed by last ranked truck 0..3 for testing/toggling the active-human mask.

units.name: color_podium_by_ranked_truck
units.description: For each of the top three ranks, choose its CGRAM destination and copy eight palette bytes selected by the ranked truck ID. Preserve caller status.

units.name: podium_cgram_destinations
units.description: Three CGRAM destination bytes, visited with descending podium index 2..0.

units.name: draw_podium_awards_and_names
units.description:
For the top three ranks, apply rank-indexed awards, render award digits and copy each truck's three name characters into the podium tilemap.
Draw winning time and stored track record through helpers, then compare the new time with the stored record to set the pending record-update flag.
Amounts are frontend/accounting units; exact currency scaling follows the separate BCD money helper.

units.name: compare_record_time_low_words
units.description: When the higher race-time component ties, compare the remaining packed time against the track record and take the faster-time path on borrow.

units.name: clear_new_track_record_flag
units.description: Clear the pending record-update flag when the winning time does not beat the stored track record.

units.name: set_new_track_record_flag
units.description: Set the pending record-update flag when the comparison selects a new track record.

units.name: draw_winner_time_and_stored_record
units.description:
Draw the winner's three name characters and packed decimal time digits into the awards tilemap.
Internal $ABC2 draws the selected track's stored three-character record holder and decimal time from parallel RAM arrays. Tile attributes and the separator tile are fixed.

units.name: podium_award_values
units.description: Three award bytes selected by descending podium index 2..0. The fourth adjacent byte is generic data; a consumer and membership in this award array remain unresolved.

units.name: podium_vram_destination_pairs
units.description: Two parallel three-word VRAM destination arrays. Rank 0..2 selects corresponding words with separate low/high-byte reads.

units.name: poll_start_or_splash_timeout
units.description:
Combine all four controller Start bits. Without Start, decrement the 16-bit splash timer and return its sign through the resulting flags.
On Start, the RAM signature decides whether to keep timing the initial splash or jump to frontend reentry, which restores the saved stack.

units.name: convert_inactive_truck_money_to_nitro
units.description:
For each inactive truck with a nonzero money record, decrement its low money byte and increment BCD nitro stock up to $80, refreshing the frontend display after each increment.
Repeat until its balance is exhausted or the stock limit is reached. Human-controlled slots are skipped; preserve status.

units.name: prepare_player_shop_frontend
units.description: Clear the frontend page selector, inhibit race uploads and initialize window, palette and font resources. The following fragment resets shop cursors and input state.

units.name: initialize_shop_players_and_cursors
units.description:
Reset shop choice/row/column/input bytes for two players. Invert the selected player-choice bits to obtain the initial done mask.
For each unfinished player, position its cursor using the shared geometry helper. This shop done mask is distinct from the active truck mask.

units.name: select_second_shop_page
units.description: Use player page one for the second shop grid's common cursor renderer.

units.name: clear_shop_maps_and_choose_heading
units.description: Select the frontend layer mask, clear two background maps and select page-specific heading text. The alternate heading fragment supplies its rectangle destination and descriptor.

units.name: select_alternate_shop_rectangle
units.description: Select the alternate shop rectangle destination and descriptor before joining the shared rectangle draw.

units.name: draw_shop_display_and_fade_in
units.description:
Draw heading text, initialize both nine-sprite cursor groups and refresh money/stock display fields.
Prime the five-field upgrade redraw service through six calls, enable video updates, request shop audio and fade in.

units.name: set_shop_loop_widths
units.description: Establish byte accumulator and index widths for the shop input loop.

units.name: run_shop_input_frame
units.description: Each frame refresh money, one upgrade field, controller state and both players' shop handlers. Repeat until the two-bit done mask is three.

units.name: leave_completed_shop_page
units.description: Upload final display state, wait a frame and inhibit race video updates. Request transition audio and start the expanding window effect.

units.name: advance_shop_page
units.description: Request frontend audio, increment the current page selector and compare with the page limit. Another page reenters setup; otherwise return.

units.name: reload_next_shop_page
units.description: Jump to the shared shop setup entry while retaining the incremented page selector.

units.name: return_completed_shop
units.description: Return to the caller after all required shop pages finish.

units.name: shop_continue_cursor_tilewords
units.description: Nine little-endian sprite tile/attribute words staged into OAM with source stride two and destination stride four.

units.name: text_glyphs_2db4
units.description: Glyph-index stream through its first $FF terminator, selected by an explicit source pointer passed to the single-tile text consumer. Literal glyph codes retain the local font encoding; no unsupported text identity is assigned.

units.name: test_player_one_shop_done
units.description: Skip player one's handler once its done-mask bit is set. Otherwise use player index zero.

units.name: return_shop_handler
units.description: Return from the completed shop operation.

units.name: repeat_player_one_shop_direction
units.description:
Release resets the direction-repeat timer. A held direction counts down, then reloads an eight-frame interval and tests movement bits.
The input byte also carries the separate purchase/confirm bit handled later.

units.name: move_player_one_shop_cursor
units.description:
