Convert direction bits to deltas, update bounded row/column coordinates and map them through cursor geometry tables.
Internal $AE22 takes player index Y and sets the first OAM cursor origin; expand it into nine sprites through the shared geometry helper.

units.name: detect_player_one_shop_confirm_edge
units.description: Rotate the confirm bit into history and require a new press. Convert row/column to a six-slot item index; slot five means Start Next Race.

units.name: finish_player_one_shop_selection
units.description: Draw the completion text, set player one's done bit and hide its nine cursor sprites.

units.name: return_or_select_player_one_money_record
units.description: The first RTS returns without a new confirmation. Internal $AE89 selects the six-byte money record using the current page; its alternate setup selects the second wallet at byte offset twelve.

units.name: select_second_wallet
units.description: Select byte offset twelve, the second player's wallet block, before checking affordability.

units.name: test_player_one_purchase_funds
units.description: A nonzero upper money byte proves sufficient funds; otherwise the low byte is compared with the item cost in an adjoining fragment.

units.name: check_low_wallet_digits
units.description: Compare the lower wallet digits with the selected item's cost. Return immediately if insufficient; otherwise fall through to the purchase path.

units.name: select_player_one_upgrade_slot
units.description: Save the money-record offset and convert item index to a four-truck upgrade-array offset, adjusted for the current frontend page.

units.name: advance_shop_redraw_field
units.description: Advance by two to the companion shop redraw field.

units.name: buy_player_one_shop_item
units.description:
Reject purchases at the per-item cap. Otherwise increment the selected upgrade/stock byte in decimal mode and subtract the item cost from the low money byte.
The preceding funds test establishes affordability; this fragment preserves the encoded byte arithmetic.

units.name: return_rejected_player_one_purchase
units.description: Return without changing money or upgrades when a cap or funds test rejects the purchase.

units.name: expand_first_shop_cursor_sprites
units.description: Preserve X/Y/status, then position nine shadow sprites around the first cursor origin using paired signed offset tables. Coordinates wrap as byte arithmetic.

units.name: build_shop_cursor_sprites
units.description: Preserve the caller's indices/status and expand the anchor at OAM $0224 into nine cursor sprites. Parallel signed X/Y offset tables position each four-byte OAM record around the selected grid cell.

units.name: cursor_coordinate_deltas
units.description: Two parallel nine-byte coordinate-delta arrays, added to the cursor OAM X and Y origins. The consumer visits indices 8..0.

units.name: shop_item_costs_and_caps
units.description: Five byte costs followed by five byte upgrade caps. Item=2*row+column; item 5 exits before these reads. These fields are bytes even though adjacent pair patterns resemble words.

units.name: test_player_two_shop_done
units.description: Return immediately once player two's done bit is set; otherwise select player index one.

units.name: repeat_and_move_player_two_shop_direction
units.description:
Mirror player one's eight-frame repeat handling using the second input/timer bytes, then update its row/column and derive cursor coordinates.
The next fragment finishes its grid-derived screen coordinates and expands the composite cursor before confirmation.

units.name: position_second_shop_cursor
units.description: Finish the second shop cursor's screen coordinates using the menu-grid tables, then expand its composite sprites.

units.name: detect_player_two_confirm_and_finish_slot
units.description: Require a new confirm press from player two's history byte. Select the six-slot item index; slot five draws its completion message. The adjoining done tail sets player two bit and hides all nine cursor sprites.

units.name: finish_second_shop_selection
units.description: Mark player two done and move all nine of that page's cursor sprites offscreen at Y=$F0.

units.name: buy_player_two_shop_item
units.description:
The first RTS rejects a missing confirmation. Internal $AFDC selects player two's money record, checks upper bytes or item cost and chooses its per-truck upgrade offset.
Reject items at their cap; otherwise increment stock/upgrade in decimal mode and subtract the cost. Preserve the separate player-two money/upgrade offsets.

units.name: update_shop_column_with_wrap
units.description: Add horizontal input delta to the player's two-column cursor and test bounds. The separate negative wrap selects the last column; the high-side wrap reaches zero.

units.name: set_first_player_done_bit
units.description: Select bit one before the common frontend completion-mask update.

units.name: wrap_shop_column_to_zero
units.description: Set the two-column cursor to zero after crossing its upper boundary.

units.name: update_shop_row_with_wrap
units.description: Commit the column, add vertical input delta to the three-row cursor and test bounds. Separate tails wrap below zero to two and above two to zero.

units.name: choose_shop_row_wrap_value
units.description: Use row two for negative overflow, or zero for positive overflow, before the common row store.

units.name: store_shop_row_and_return
units.description: Commit the bounded shop row for player index Y and return.

units.name: cycle_shop_upgrade_display_field
units.description:
Advance a five-field redraw cursor modulo five. Skip drawing player one after its done bit is set, and select its upgrade record using the current page.
The selected field determines tilemap destination and stock/bar display.

units.name: advance_upgrade_field
units.description: Advance the word-sized upgrade field selector to the next entry.

units.name: choose_shop_upgrade_bar_destination
units.description: Load the selected upgrade count and its tilemap destination. Zero stock skips the active bar; counts at least seven use an adjoining destination adjustment.

units.name: cap_upgrade_bar_six
units.description: Clamp the rendered upgrade bar to six units.

units.name: test_shop_upgrade_bar_count
units.description: Set the VRAM destination and distinguish one-unit stock from a multi-unit bar. The following bar body writes paired units with an odd-unit tail.

units.name: draw_upgrade_bar_pair
units.description: Write a filled two-unit tile, move the destination one row upward and repeat until fewer than two units remain. A final odd unit uses the common single-unit tile path.

units.name: draw_shop_bar_end_and_test_player_two
units.description: Write the fixed bar-end tile and check whether player two's done bit permits its corresponding field redraw.

units.name: draw_second_page_upgrade_bar
units.description: Select the second player's upgrade from the redraw field and current page. Clamp its value to six and draw paired tiles upward from the field's VRAM destination, with a separate tile for an odd final unit. Zero skips the bar.

units.name: return_shop_field_redraw
units.description: Restore the caller's status after shop upgrade-field drawing.

units.name: shop_upgrade_bar_destinations
units.description: Two parallel five-word VRAM destination arrays for the upgrade bars. The cursor wraps at five and selects words with twice its value.

units.name: load_podium_resources
units.description:
Clear the background map, disable HDMA and DMA podium graphics ($4000 bytes), palette ($200 bytes) and map ($640 bytes) from bank seven.
Use mode one for VRAM and byte mode for CGRAM, restoring caller status after all transfers.

units.name: begin_attract_graphics_upload
units.description: Save status and select 16-bit indices. The following width-dependent immediate is unresolved and remains outside this fragment.

units.name: upload_attract_display_dma
units.description:
Continue the status-preserving initializer: clear the VRAM window, disable HDMA and use DMA channel1.
Transfer$4D00graphics bytes from$08:8000to VRAM word0,256palette bytes from$08:D340to CGRAM0, then1536tilemap bytes from$08:CD00to VRAM$4040.
Finish by clearing the two VRAM windows at$4800and$4C00. The saved status was pushed in the preceding classified prefix.

units.name: begin_driver_graphics_upload
units.description: Save status and select 16-bit indices before the driver graphics setup. The following immediate boundary is independently classified only where its context is established.

units.name: upload_driver_frontend_tiles
units.description: Clear the main background map, disable HDMA and DMA $4DA0 bytes from $098000 into VRAM. Restore the status saved by the upload prefix.

units.name: configure_driver_palette_dma
units.description: Save status and configure channel one for byte writes to CGRAM from bank nine, starting at palette entry zero. The next fragment supplies source/length.

units.name: upload_driver_frontend_palette
units.description: DMA $100 palette bytes from $09D410. On the alternate frontend page, replace a $40-byte palette subset from $09D158. Restore status.

units.name: prepare_shop_graphics_and_heading
units.description: Save status, upload driver graphics/palette and select 16-bit indices for the following heading rectangle.

units.name: select_driver_heading_map
units.description: Set VRAM destination $4020 and the low word of the heading-map source pointer. The next fragment supplies its bank and descriptor.

units.name: draw_driver_heading_and_test_first_panel
units.description: Draw the heading from bank nine, then test the first player-choice bit on this frontend page to select its panel variant.

units.name: draw_alternate_frontend_rectangle
units.description: Prepare bank $09 source $CF60 and its rectangle descriptor, draw it to VRAM $4121, then join the shared frontend display continuation.

units.name: draw_continued_first_driver_panel
units.description: Draw the first continued-driver rectangle from $09D198. Select a $20-byte palette replacement based on the frontend page.

units.name: upload_alternate_continued_panel_palette
units.description: Replace the selected CGRAM subset with $20 bytes from $09D3D0 for the alternate frontend page.

units.name: draw_second_driver_panel
units.description: Test the second player-choice bit and draw the standard second panel if it is clear. Otherwise branch to the continued-panel variant.

units.name: draw_continued_second_driver_panel
units.description: Draw the shared continued-driver map into the second panel using its own rectangle descriptor and VRAM destination.

units.name: load_second_page_palette
units.description: Choose one of two player-page palettes in bank $09 and copy its 32 bytes into CGRAM starting at color $50.

units.name: clear_frontend_text_map_and_return
units.description: Clear the map at VRAM $4800 and restore the display-wrapper caller's status.

units.name: driver_heading_rectangle_descriptor
units.description:
Ten little-endian words for draw_remapped_tile_rectangle: width/flags, height and eight palette substitutions.
Width=32, height=7; width bit 15 permits palette remapping. The caller supplies the separate source pointer and VRAM destination.

units.name: continued_driver_rectangle
units.description:
Ten little-endian words for draw_remapped_tile_rectangle: width/flags, height and eight palette substitutions.
Width=14, height=18; width bit 15 permits palette remapping. The caller supplies the separate source pointer and VRAM destination.

units.name: driver1_panel_rectangle_descriptor
units.description:
Ten little-endian words for draw_remapped_tile_rectangle: width/flags, height and eight palette substitutions.
Width=14, height=18; width bit 15 permits palette remapping. The caller supplies the separate source pointer and VRAM destination.

units.name: alternate_player2_shop_rectangle
units.description:
Ten little-endian words for draw_remapped_tile_rectangle: width/flags, height and eight palette substitutions.
Width=14, height=18; width bit 15 permits palette remapping. The caller supplies the separate source pointer and VRAM destination.

units.name: driver2_panel_rectangle_descriptor
units.description:
Ten little-endian words for draw_remapped_tile_rectangle: width/flags, height and eight palette substitutions.
Width=14, height=18; width bit 15 permits palette remapping. The caller supplies the separate source pointer and VRAM destination.

units.name: prepare_standard_driver_panels
units.description: Upload driver graphics and palette, then establish the widths used by the two standard-panel rectangle calls.

units.name: draw_two_standard_driver_panels
units.description: Draw the common panel map twice, at the two player destinations with separate rectangle descriptors. Restore caller status.

units.name: draw_inline_driver_panel_heading
units.description:
Draw a fixed driver-panel tile heading at VRAM word $408A using the byte-tile renderer and the inline FF-terminated string following this stub.
Native E=0 is required; REP10 establishes X16 for both literal arguments, independently of M. The DB00 text association follows the renderer interface and exact inline terminator, rather than an observed call. This stub leaves index width 16; renderer preserves the status it receives. Natural entry remains unresolved.

units.name: inline_driver_panel_heading_tiles
units.description:
Inline byte-tile string for draw_inline_driver_panel_heading. Y points at its first byte under the inferred DB00 interface; the renderer emits each tile with attribute $20 and stops before emitting $FF.
The first $FF is the twelfth byte. The terminator and independently established next routine bound this object exactly; character spelling is not asserted.

units.name: disable_window_masks
units.description: Clear the three window-mask selection registers while preserving status. This does not disable HDMA by itself.

units.name: setup_hdma_window_and_build_scanlines
units.description:
Configure channel seven for indirect HDMA to the two window position registers, using bank-zero tables and WRAM bank $7E. Prime both alternating buffers before enabling it.
Internal $B4C6 chooses a shape-source pointer, toggles the scanline buffer, initializes closed-window pairs $8081 and transforms boundary samples using the transition extent.
Mode 7 multiplication maps shape distance from its vertical center onto scanlines. Samples outside the byte range skip output for that row. Left/right boundaries are then scaled around the horizontal center.

units.name: skip_window_row_above_screen
units.description: Advance past a shape boundary pair when subtracting the scaled vertical distance underflows. This belongs to the HDMA window builder, not score processing.

units.name: place_window_row_below_center
units.description: Add the scaled vertical distance to the window's vertical center. Overflow skips the row instead of wrapping it onscreen.

units.name: skip_window_row_below_screen
units.description: Advance past a boundary pair after vertical overflow; share the window builder's next-sample tail.

units.name: scale_left_window_boundary
units.description:
Convert the computed scanline to a byte-pair buffer offset, choosing the active half. Scale the signed left-boundary sample around the horizontal center using the transition extent.
Positive overflow or negative underflow clamps through separate tails; output is repeated across four rows.

units.name: select_negative_window_edge
units.description: Use $FF as the clipped window edge before the common window-buffer store.

units.name: scale_negative_left_boundary
units.description: Negate the signed shape sample, multiply its magnitude by the extent and subtract the product from the horizontal center.

units.name: clamp_left_window_boundary
units.description: Use one as the left boundary when the horizontal calculation falls outside its supported range.

units.name: store_left_and_scale_right_boundary
units.description: Repeat the computed left boundary over four scanlines. Read the paired right sample, scale its positive magnitude and add the horizontal center; overflow selects the right-edge clamp.

units.name: clamp_right_window_boundary
units.description: Use $FF as the right boundary after positive overflow.

units.name: scale_negative_right_boundary
units.description: Scale a negative right-boundary sample by magnitude and subtract from the horizontal center. An underflow clamp is outside this classified fragment.

units.name: select_zero_window_edge
units.description: Use zero as the clipped window edge before the common window-buffer store.

units.name: finish_window_boundary_pair
units.description:
Repeat the right boundary over four scanlines, advance the shape sample and continue until $100 source bytes have been consumed.
Restore closed-window pairs after the last emitted row and return with caller status. Both shape bytes and physical WRAM buffer offsets have separate roles.

units.name: window_hdma_descriptor_pair
units.description: Two seven-byte indirect HDMA descriptors, selected on alternating window buffers. Each has two $FF line-count entries followed by WRAM pointers and a zero terminator. The consumer installs the channel bank separately; pointers are not ROM addresses.

units.name: window_shape_source_records
units.description: Three records in frontend/race/pause selector order. Each record stores a source bank byte followed by a little-endian address. The window builder indexes three times the explicit shape selector.

units.name: initialize_money_and_record_defaults
units.description:
Clear four six-byte decimal money records and give each a one in its third digit. Internal $B63F copies default track-record names/times, high-score totals/names/order and truck names from bounded ROM arrays.
The copy lengths are $30,$20,$3C,$1E,$0A and $0C bytes respectively; later consumers establish the record interpretations.

units.name: default_track_record_names
units.description: Sixteen three-byte record-holder names copied to RAM $06F8. The record display indexes these by 3*trackID.

units.name: default_track_record_times
units.description: Sixteen packed-decimal two-byte record times copied to RAM $06D8. Display and result comparison use this parallel track table.

units.name: default_truck_names
units.description: Four three-byte driver names copied to RAM $0600 before name entry replaces selected records.

units.name: truck_money_record_offsets
units.description: Four byte offsets 0,6,12,18 into the six-digit money records, selected by truck ID 0..3.

units.name: add_award_to_money_digit_five
units.description:
Add input A low byte to byte 5 of the selected six-byte money record, using the truck-to-record offset table. Carry/borrow normalization is performed separately by normalize_six_money_digits; this addition assumes decimal clear.
PHX saves X at its incoming width; PHP/SEP30 then selects 8-bit body registers. PLP restores the original X width before PLX, so X is fully restored. PLX changes N/Z after PLP; do not treat all returned flags as preserved. SEP30 also clears Y high if incoming native X16.
DP/DB do not determine instruction boundaries. Named state and table references assume DB00/DP0000; natural entry remains unresolved.

units.name: add_award_to_money_digit_four
units.description:
Add input A low byte to byte 4 of the selected six-byte money record, using the truck-to-record offset table. Carry/borrow normalization is performed separately by normalize_six_money_digits; this addition assumes decimal clear.
PHX saves X at its incoming width; PHP/SEP30 then selects 8-bit body registers. PLP restores the original X width before PLX, so X is fully restored. PLX changes N/Z after PLP; do not treat all returned flags as preserved. SEP30 also clears Y high if incoming native X16.
DP/DB do not determine instruction boundaries. Named state and table references assume DB00/DP0000; natural entry remains unresolved.

units.name: add_award_to_money_digits
units.description:
Add byte A to the low money digit selected by the current truck ID and a six-byte-record offset table. Normalization is separate.
PHX saves original-width X; PLP restores that width before PLX. X is restored, but final PLX replaces N/Z. SEP30 clears Y high if incoming native X16; full Y/status preservation is not promised.

units.name: normalize_six_money_digits
units.description:
Walk the selected six-digit money record from least significant digit to most significant. Carry values at least ten into the preceding digit; borrow negative values in the opposite direction.
Store each digit in 0..9. The highest-digit overflow behavior follows the encoded guard and is retained rather than generalized to arbitrary precision. Preserve X/Y/status.

units.name: refresh_two_players_money
units.description: Normalize both truck money records for the frontend page, then choose their six-byte source record for conditional rendering.

units.name: advance_placement_record_pair
units.description: Advance twelve bytes to the next pair of six-byte placement records.

units.name: draw_money_for_joined_players
units.description: Set the money source pointer and draw the first player's amount only when joined. Test the second joined bit for its separate display path.

units.name: draw_second_placement_record
units.description: Advance the source pointer by six bytes and draw the companion placement field at VRAM $4974.

units.name: draw_six_digit_money_field
units.description:
The first tail restores the caller's status. Internal $B7C6 clears nine tiles, suppresses leading zero digits from a six-digit source pointer and appends two zero tiles.
Thus stored money units render with two extra decimal zeros. The indirect pointer uses bank-zero RAM and the selected VRAM destination comes from X.

units.name: default_high_score_digits
units.description: Ten six-byte most-significant-first decimal digit records copied to RAM $0578. The high-score insertion helper compares them lexicographically.

units.name: default_high_score_names
units.description: Ten three-byte high-score names copied to RAM $05B4, indexed by the same storage IDs as the score records.

units.name: default_high_score_order
units.description: Ten storage IDs copied to RAM $05D2. Insertion reorders IDs while keeping the six-digit and three-character records in parallel storage.

units.name: insert_truck_totals_into_high_scores
units.description:
Normalize each truck's money record and compare it against ten ordered high-score records.
Internal $B88E compares six digits most significant first, copies a qualifying total and three-character name into the replaced storage slot, then moves its ID into the ranked order list.
The ranking array holds indirection IDs rather than copying all score records during shifts.

units.name: draw_highscore_rows
units.description:
Preserve status and upload the paired-tile font, then draw the terminated heading at VRAM$480B.
Use high_score_order to select ten six-byte score records. Stage their stored digits in scratch, suppress leading zero pairs and draw six two-tile digits with attribute$20.
Append the paired border tiles, then make a second pass drawing each selected three-character name as paired glyphs. Row destinations are independent score/name word tables.

units.name: highscore_heading_tiles
units.description: Paired-tile high-score heading. The text helper reads byte glyph indices through the first$FFterminator; exactly10bytes belong to this string.

units.name: highscore_score_row_destinations
units.description: Ten little-endian VRAM word destinations, indexed by displayed row0..9. Score and name passes use separate tables.

units.name: highscore_name_row_destinations
units.description: Ten little-endian VRAM word destinations, indexed by displayed row0..9. Score and name passes use separate tables.

units.name: paired_text_glyphs_3a43
units.description: Glyph-index stream through its first $FF terminator, selected by an explicit source pointer passed to the paired-tile text consumer. Literal glyph codes retain the local font encoding; no unsupported text identity is assigned.

units.name: text_glyphs_3a8a
units.description: Glyph-index stream through its first $FF terminator, selected by an explicit source pointer passed to the single-tile text consumer. Literal glyph codes retain the local font encoding; no unsupported text identity is assigned.

units.name: paired_text_glyphs_3aa0
units.description: Glyph-index stream through its first $FF terminator, selected by an explicit source pointer passed to the paired-tile text consumer. Literal glyph codes retain the local font encoding; no unsupported text identity is assigned.

units.name: name_entry_text_records
units.description: Four stride-four records: VRAM destination word then CPU-bank-zero source pointer word. The initializer visits offsets 12,8,4,0 and calls the paired-glyph text helper.

units.name: draw_terminated_tile_text
units.description:
Draw byte tile IDs until $FF, with fixed $2000 attributes and horizontal VRAM increment.
Internal $BADC uses vertical VRAM increment and doubles each character into a two-tile pair, stepping the base destination for the next character. Caller Y points into bank-zero mapped source; preserve status.

units.name: draw_seven_large_text_rows
units.description: Call the paired-tile text renderer seven times, advancing VRAM by $40 words per terminated source row. Increment Y past each $FF separator.

units.name: begin_clear_name_entry_panel
units.description: Wait a frame, set the requested VRAM destination and configure word writes before the rectangular clear body.

units.name: clear_name_entry_panel
units.description: Clear an eleven-column by fourteen-row tile rectangle using $2000 blank words and a 32-word row stride. Restore caller status.

units.name: begin_player_selection
units.description: Inhibit race uploads, reset frontend page and joined masks, fade out and reset background scroll latches/window masks. Subsequent setup establishes selection audio and per-page state.

units.name: initialize_name_entry_pages
units.description:
Request selection audio and process each configured frontend page. Internal $BB99 resets join/name/cursor state, initializes both temporary names and starts the join countdown.
Clear maps, draw the panel heading and seven-row character layout, then draw page-specific instructions. Temporary names store character bytes in the paired-tile text format.

units.name: draw_alternate_name_page_extra_text
units.description:
Draw the additional terminated glyph stream at CPU $BA9E to VRAM word $491B through the existing byte-text helper, then fall through into the already classified continuation.
The preceding caller establishes native M8/X16 and DB/DP zero; the helper preserves this contract.

units.name: run_name_entry_frame
units.description:
Initialize sprite shadows and fade in. Every frame redraw joined players' temporary names, countdown, controller words, cursor sprites and both join/name handlers.
When both done bits are set, copy finalized names, upload the final display and inhibit further race updates before transitioning.

units.name: send_frontend_sound_e8
units.description: Send command $E803 to the audio ports, run the frontend delay/transition helper and restore 16-bit accumulator mode.

units.name: send_name_entry_audio_ack
units.description: Write$0101to APU ports2/3, restore the byte accumulator contract and return. This completes the earlier name-entry/audio helper.

units.name: commit_names_and_tick_join_countdown
units.description:
Copy alternating bytes from each temporary paired-tile name into the two three-byte final-name records for this page.
Internal $BCFF displays the join countdown for unjoined players, decrements it every fourth frame and marks absent players done at expiry. Internal $BD63 clears completed panels and hides their cursor sprites.

units.name: hide_first_name_cursor_pair
units.description: Hide the first player's two name-entry cursor sprites by setting both screen-Y bytes to $F0.

units.name: clear_completed_second_name_panel
units.description: If player two is done, clear its name-entry panel before its cursor hide tail.

units.name: hide_second_name_cursor_pair
units.description: Hide the second player's two cursor sprites by setting their screen-Y bytes to $F0.

units.name: test_first_player_join_edge
units.description:
The first tail restores status after hiding completed cursors. Internal $BD96 skips players already joined/done and detects a new Select press with a history byte.
Set player one's joined bit and synchronize to the next frame before drawing its selection grid.

units.name: show_first_joined_name_grid
units.description: Draw the first player's seven-row character grid, install paired cursor tile words and position its two cursor sprites at the first grid cell.

units.name: test_second_player_join_edge
units.description:
The first RTS ends player one's join handler. Internal $BDED skips second players already joined/done and begins their independent Select-edge test.
Detect its new Select press through the second history byte, set its joined bit and wait a frame before drawing the second name-entry panel.

units.name: draw_second_name_page
units.description: Draw the second name-entry page at VRAM $4954 with its shared rectangle helper.

units.name: initialize_name_entry_cursor_sprites
units.description: Initialize the two name-editor cursor tilewords and X positions, then Y positions16pixels apart. This tail falls through into the existing editor body; it is not a separate returning routine.

units.name: handle_first_player_name_input
units.description:
Return from the second join handler, then at $BE44 process player one only while joined and unfinished. Release clears its repeat timer; held movement repeats every eight frames.
Decode direction bits and begin the five-column character-grid wrap.

units.name: wrap_first_name_grid_cursor
units.description: Wrap player one's column modulo five and row modulo seven, including negative-direction wrap to the last column/row.

units.name: position_first_name_grid_cursor
units.description: Index the 35-cell coordinate tables with 5*row+column. Offset the first player's paired cursor sprites by its panel origin.

units.name: edit_first_player_name
units.description:
Preview the selected character at the current two-byte temporary-name position. On a new B press, ordinary characters advance the cursor up to three characters.
Negative grid tokens are controls: $FF sets done and hides the panel; the other negative token backs up one character when possible. Unconfirmed controls preview a placeholder.

units.name: handle_second_player_name_input
units.description: Mirror player one's joined/done guard and eight-frame direction repeat using the second input/timer bytes. Begin its character-grid movement; the adjoining wrap fragment bounds the column to 0..4 and row to 0..6.

units.name: wrap_second_name_grid
units.description: Wrap the second player's name-grid column into 0..4 and row into 0..6 after applying the pending movement deltas.

units.name: position_second_name_grid_cursor
units.description: Index the shared 35-cell grid and position the second player's cursor pair using its own panel origin. The separate character editor previews, accepts or backspaces the selected character on a new button edge.

units.name: edit_second_player_name
units.description: Preview the selected grid character in the second player's temporary name, using $2A for special cells. On a fresh button edge, negative grid values either accept the name ($FF) or backspace; ordinary characters advance the cursor up to byte six. The paired increments reflect the interleaved character storage.

units.name: temporary_name_defaults
units.description: Ten initial name bytes copied to both temporary-name buffers, with descending index 9..0. Glyph identities remain literal.

units.name: name_editor_cell_tables
units.description: Three parallel 35-byte arrays: X position, Y position and glyph. Cell=5*row+column with rows 0..6 and columns 0..4; the shop shares a subset of these cells.

units.name: poll_frontend_controllers
units.description:
Copy the first two automatic joypad words into the two frontend input pairs. Both page branches currently perform the same copies.
Internal $C097 saves status and selects byte indices before the direction-table helper.
Internal direction entry SEP10 clears Y high for incoming native X16; PLP cannot recover discarded high bytes.

units.name: decode_direction_and_initialize_frontend_sprites
units.description:
Mask the four direction bits and use parallel tables to return signed horizontal/vertical deltas in $11/$13.
Internal $C0AA hides 128 OAM entries and sixteen sprite-array entries, sets large-size bits and repacks the shadow. Internal $C0DB uploads two $800-byte frontend font spans and clears the text map.

units.name: track_eight_overlay_descriptor
units.description: Twenty-byte rectangle descriptor copied into rectangle_width_flags and its following workspace. First words give width/flags and row count; sixteen following bytes remap tile palette nibbles. The row consumer bounds the source rectangle.

units.name: track_fourteen_overlay_descriptor
units.description: Twenty-byte rectangle descriptor: width/flags word, row-count word and sixteen palette-remap bytes. Shared by both track-fourteen overlays; exact source lengths follow the nested row/column counts.

units.name: initialize_race_hud_tiles
units.description:
Upload $2000 HUD graphics bytes from $07B600 and clear the text map. Fill two 64-word strips with the border tile.
The direction flag selects the reversed-track presentation path; the track-specific overlay continuation is described separately.

units.name: draw_track_specific_overlays
units.description: Draw a bank $0D tile overlay for track eight, or two smaller overlays for track fourteen. Each uses the common count-bounded rectangle format and an explicit source-bank contract.

units.name: draw_track_title_banner_and_hud_sprites
units.description:
Draw the common banner at a track-indexed destination, then draw the track title from parallel pointer/rectangle/destination tables.
Build sixteen HUD sprites from fixed relative positions, per-track anchors and attribute bytes. Clear the packed decimal race timer after setup.

units.name: update_lap_and_nitro_hud_digits
units.description: Write four lap digits and eight BCD nitro digits into their OAM tile fields. Test the high race-time digit before the decimal timer update.

units.name: test_race_timer_saturation
units.description: Compare the middle BCD timer byte with $99 before allowing another update at the upper display limit.

units.name: advance_and_draw_race_timer
units.description:
Add decimal $16 to the three-byte timer, propagating carry in decimal mode. Draw three visible decimal nibbles into HUD sprite tile IDs.
The step is an encoded timing unit, not independently established wall-clock milliseconds.

units.name: track_hud_layout_tables
units.description:
Sixteen title source triples, sixteen descriptor pointers, seven ten-word rectangles, sixteen VRAM destinations and HUD sprite/anchor arrays.
The final ten-word rectangle describes the common banner. Source and destination fields are distinct CPU pointers and VRAM word addresses; labels below retain those roles.

units.name: upload_text_base_palette
units.description: DMA $20 bytes from $08E1E0 to the first CGRAM entries using channel one. Preserve status.

units.name: upload_frontend_cursor_tiles_and_palette
units.description: Copy $400 sprite bytes from $08DDE0 to VRAM $6200 and $40 palette bytes from $08E200 to the upper CGRAM half. Preserve status.

units.name: draw_remapped_tile_rectangle
units.description:
Inputs: X is VRAM destination, Y points to a twenty-byte descriptor, and $54..$56 is a 24-bit map source. Copy width/height and eight palette-remap words into RAM.
Draw width*height words with 32-word VRAM row stride. Width bit 15 bypasses palette substitution; otherwise replace tile palette bits 10..12 through the eight-entry remap.
Advance only the source low word by two per tile; bank crossing is not generalized. Preserve caller status.

units.name: load_track_object_placements
units.description:
Use the track's sixteen-slot pointer table to read a count word followed by six-byte X/Y/height records. Populate parallel object arrays and clear each animation state. A negative X ends early.
Initialize track-specific object services, project objects and reset pickup/counter/award state. Exact count-bounded source structure is independent of live reachability.

units.name: dispatch_random_pickup_state
units.description: A zero pickup state permits a random spawn attempt; active states branch to collision or expiry handling.

units.name: gate_random_pickup_spawn
units.description: Generate a random byte. A zero result takes an adjoining alternate path; ordinary nonzero results continue selecting a spawn record.

units.name: skip_inactive_pickup
units.description: Jump to the common inactive-pickup continuation.

units.name: choose_track_pickup_record
units.description:
Index four six-byte spawn records per track using 24*trackID+6*randomSlot. Load pickup X/Y/height and alternate its type using frame parity.
A per-type counter at least four suppresses the spawn. The full selector table extent is a separate structural question.

units.name: activate_random_pickup
units.description: Set pickup type to frame parity plus one, then project its world coordinates into its sprite shadow.

units.name: return_after_pickup_spawn_attempt
units.description: Jump to the pickup service's status-restoring return.

units.name: dispatch_pickup_expiry
units.description: Jump to the active pickup's expiry/animation path.

units.name: test_pickup_near_one_truck
units.description:
Types below three test one truck per frame, selected by frame parity modulo four. Require pickup X within a $300-wide interval and Y within a $500-high interval.
The following award body saturates the type count, updates nitro or pending award digits and refreshes its sprites.

units.name: award_collected_pickup
units.description: Saturate the selected pickup type's collection count at four and combine it with the type's base award. Values below seven add BCD nitro, preserving the old amount on overflow; higher values add pending award digits. Send the matching race sound and refresh pickup sprites.

units.name: set_pickup_lifetime_eighty
units.description: Install an80-tick pickup lifetime after the drawing helper returns; fall through into the existing pickup update.

units.name: animate_and_expire_pickup
units.description: Every fourth frame move two pickup sprite Y bytes upward. Decrement lifetime each update; on expiry hide both sprites and clear pickup state.

units.name: return_pickup_service
units.description: Restore status and return from pickup handling.

units.name: pickup_spawn_records
units.description: Sixteen track groups of four six-byte spawn records. Each record contains little-endian world X, world Y and height. The consumer uses 24*track+6*(RNG&3); all four choices have bounded fields even when a choice is not naturally observed.

units.name: project_pickup_sprite
units.description:
Select the pickup tile word from its state, project world X/Y/height through the shared terrain projection and offset into screen coordinates.
Hide a separate shadow byte at $122D, then test for a multi-sprite type. The extra path selects an award-state tileword and centers its sprite pair.

units.name: draw_extra_pickup_tile
units.description: Select the pickup tileword for award states above the base set and center its two-sprite display around the stored X coordinate.

units.name: return_pickup_projection
units.description: Restore status after pickup screen projection.

units.name: pickup_award_bases_and_tiles
units.description: Two little-endian award-base words, followed by eight sprite tilewords for award states 3..10. The previous per-type collection count is capped at three for award selection; type bases map it into the two award families.

units.name: pickup_state_tilewords
units.description: Ten little-endian tilewords for active states 1..10, indexed by 2*state relative to the consumer base. The preceding state-zero word is outside this classified window; do not assume it shares the active format.

units.name: initialize_sequence_objects
units.description:
Select a pointer using the full track-order slot and initialize up to six word-indexed object entries. Clear each type before testing its six-byte source record.
Nonzero records enter the separate object initializer; the common tail preserves the exact six-byte stride.

units.name: initialize_dynamic_object_record
units.description: Copy a six-byte X/Y/height record into a dynamic object slot, initialize type one and a random use count 0..7, clear animation/timer and project its first sprite. The saved source index resumes the surrounding six-record loop.

units.name: advance_sequence_object_record
units.description: Advance the source by six bytes and the object destination by one word, repeating for six slots. Restore status.

units.name: dynamic_object_record_pointers
units.description: Sixty-four little-endian CPU-bank-zero pointers indexed by the masked track-order slot (slot&$3F). Each supported target is a fixed six-record object group; pointer identity alone does not establish runtime selection.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_00
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_01
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_02
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_03
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_04
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_05
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_06
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_07
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_08
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_09
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_10
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_11
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_12
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_13
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_14
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_15
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: dynamic_object_group_16
units.description: Six fixed six-byte records, each little-endian world X, world Y and height. A zero X leaves the slot inactive but the reserved Y/height fields still belong to its record. The loader walks six slots; the record pointer comes from the 64-entry track-order table.

units.name: scan_dynamic_objects_against_truck
units.description: Select one truck per frame and scan six dynamic-object slots. Zero type skips the slot; active entries continue through animation/collision handling.

units.name: animate_dynamic_object_and_resolve_contact
units.description:
Special animation states permit contact tests against the selected truck. Bound X and Y separation, with type-specific vertical adjustment.
Type one starts a timed response and stops truck motion; other types advance state or react only to a moving truck. Request contact audio for the first response.
Use animation state to select the OAM tile/attribute word, add a timed palette bit and decrement animation every fourth frame. Exact object game identities remain uncertain.

units.name: update_type_one_object_lifetime
units.description:
For type one, decrement its timer, restore its idle tile at expiry and reduce a remaining-use counter. Exhausted objects advance type.
While active, hold a response animation and adjust sprite Y using a timer-indexed table. Other object types bypass this lifetime-specific logic.

units.name: advance_dynamic_object_scan
units.description: Restore the next descending word object index, repeat through six slots and restore caller status.

units.name: dynamic_object_height_adjustments
units.description: Three signed little-endian vertical adjustment words for active dynamic types 1..3. Type zero bypasses the lookup; type three is terminal in the supported transition chain.

units.name: dynamic_object_reaction_y_deltas
units.description: Forty-four signed byte displacements indexed by the decremented reaction timer, 0..43. Contact arms $2C, then service decrements before reading; a negative timer skips the read.

units.name: dynamic_object_animation_tiles
units.description: Thirty-five little-endian tilewords indexed by animation 0..$22. Initialization selects zero, event writers select $11/$1D/$22 and service decrements only nonzero values.

units.name: test_special_surface_contact
units.description: Require the truck contact marker and a high terrain-control nibble of $F before the special surface response. The response tests animation state, slows the working speed and positions the contact sprite.

units.name: test_pickup_contact_animation
units.description: For the selected truck, only active animation states $12 or $17 take the special effect path. Halve a nonnegative working speed and copy the effect's screen position through the shared helper.

units.name: set_contact_effect_animation_nineteen
units.description: Set the indexed truck contact-effect animation cursor to19and jump to the shared continuation. Physical classification of the state assignment is independent of natural contact coverage.

units.name: sound_and_slow_pickup_contact
units.description: Send race sound $0802, halve a nonnegative working speed and position the contact sprite through the shared helper.

units.name: set_contact_effect_animation_ten
units.description: Set the indexed truck contact-effect animation cursor to10and fall through to the shared continuation.

units.name: return_special_surface_test
units.description: Restore status and return when no special surface action applies.

units.name: position_contact_effect_sprite
units.description: Use current_truck_index to copy the truck's projected X/Y from the sorted sprite staging arrays into its contact-effect OAM record. Convert the byte/word indices separately.

units.name: initialize_track_three_objects
units.description: Only track three enters the following special-object initializer; other tracks return through the separate status tail. The adjacent initializer expands its three parallel coordinate pairs into sprite staging and OAM.

units.name: initialize_track_three_sprites
units.description: Expand three parallel X/Y table entries into the track-specific sprite staging records and a second OAM group sixteen pixels higher. Tilewords and attributes differ between the two groups.

units.name: return_track_three_initializer
units.description: Restore status for the track-three object initializer.

units.name: track_three_sprite_coordinates
units.description: Parallel three-byte screen-X and screen-Y arrays. Two three-iteration loops expand these into sprite staging and a second OAM group; the second group is sixteen pixels higher.

units.name: initialize_track_zero_objects
units.description: Zero the accumulator high byte and test track ID zero before its special object setup. The adjacent setup loads the selected count-prefixed placement records.

units.name: load_composite_object_placements
units.description: Resolve the track's placement pointer, read its count and copy count-bounded X/Y/height records into parallel composite-object arrays. Clear each timer; negative X skips the remaining activation path. Then invoke the common projection/draw routine.

units.name: return_track_zero_initializer
units.description: Restore status for the track-zero object initializer.

units.name: test_track_zero_object_service
units.description: Run the following special-object renderer only on track zero; all other tracks restore status and return.

units.name: project_track_zero_composite_objects
units.description:
Project each special object's world X/Y/height, select a six-byte sprite tuple from its animation index and store three tile/attribute words.
The following continuation writes the three-sprite projection, services reaction timers and tests truck proximity before advancing to the next count-bounded object.

units.name: update_composite_object_contact
units.description: Finish projecting each object into three horizontally adjacent sprites. Once per four frames, decrement its reaction timer. When idle, test one moving truck against the object's fixed world-coordinate rectangle and arm a 47-tick response on contact. Advance the OAM index by twelve bytes per object.

units.name: composite_object_tile_triplets
units.description: Forty-eight animation frames, each three little-endian tilewords (six bytes). The renderer writes the words into three adjacent OAM records. Animation starts at zero, contact selects $2F and nonzero timers count down.

units.name: track_zero_composite_placement_pointer
units.description: One CPU-bank-zero little-endian pointer selected only for track zero. Other track pointer cells are outside this supported window; the selected target begins with a count word.

units.name: track_zero_composite_placements
units.description: A count word of four followed by four six-byte world-X/world-Y/height records. The loader advances by two per field, initializes parallel arrays and clears the reaction timers. The four supported records have no negative-X early terminator.

units.name: update_and_project_track_objects
units.description:
Run track-zero, pickup and dynamic-object services first. Then project the count-bounded placement objects and select their sprite tile from animation state.
Every fourth frame decrement nonzero animation timers. Inactive objects proceed to the nearby-truck test; word object indices and byte sprite indices advance separately.

units.name: tick_placement_object_animation
units.description: Decrement and store this placement object's nonzero animation timer.

units.name: test_placement_object_still_animating
units.description: An active animation skips another collision trigger; zero permits a new nearby-truck test.

units.name: skip_placement_object_collision
units.description: Jump to the common next-object tail while this object's animation is active.

units.name: test_moving_truck_near_placement_object
units.description: Select one truck per frame. Ignore a zero low-seven-bit movement value, then bound X separation around the placement object. Preserve sprite index across the test.

units.name: trigger_placement_object_animation
units.description: Check the second coordinate interval; an accepted moving truck starts the placement object's $37-tick animation.

units.name: advance_placement_object_scan
units.description: Restore the sprite index, advance word object and byte sprite indices, and repeat until the placement count is reached. Restore caller status.

units.name: placement_reaction_tilewords
units.description: 56 little-endian animation tilewords. Placement animation initializes to zero, is assigned $37 on reaction and decrements only when nonzero; twice state selects the word.

units.name: track_object_placement_bundle
units.description:
Sixteen bank-zero record pointers followed by their count-prefixed placement lists. Each record is three little-endian words: world X, world Y and height.
The consumer reads exactly the count or stops at negative X. Counts are two through five and these records have no early negative exit. Pointer values alone were not used as extent evidence.

units.name: initialize_race_countdown_window
units.description: Enable the race color-math/window settings, choose the track's window center and shape one, send command $0F01 and initialize the countdown state/delay. Build the window and banner over frame boundaries before entering the countdown loop.

units.name: grow_countdown_window
units.description:
Wrap countdown state34back to18, update the window shape and grow extent by max(extent/16,1) until at least112.
While growing, repeat the existing countdown draw path; after reaching the threshold install a256-tick timer for the following countdown/contraction stage.

units.name: animate_postrace_countdown_frame
units.description: Wait a frame, redraw the countdown/banner and update sprite animation. Compare the countdown state with $22 to select a later transition stage.

units.name: restart_countdown_state_one
units.description: Reset the countdown state to $12 before the common restart continuation.

units.name: wait_countdown_hold_and_begin_closure
units.description: Decrement the transition hold timer while running animation frames. At zero, continue countdown drawing before the shrinking-window stage.

units.name: restart_countdown_state_two
units.description: Reset the countdown state to $12 for the alternate countdown continuation.

units.name: close_postrace_window
units.description:
Rebuild the scanline window, subtract max(extent/4,1) and repeat until the extent would become negative.
Wait for frame boundaries before disabling HDMA and returning, so its table is not cut mid-frame.

units.name: begin_race_get_ready_window
units.description:
Set color math/brightness, choose track-specific window center and initialize countdown state, delay and shape index.
Human play requests ready audio. Wait 26 frame boundaries before priming HDMA window buffers, then draw the initial countdown and banner.

units.name: expand_race_start_window
units.description: Rebuild the window each frame and grow its extent until $70. Below that threshold use extent/16 with a minimum step of one.

units.name: minimum_start_window_growth
units.description: Use a one-unit extent increment when division by sixteen yields zero.

units.name: commit_start_window_growth_and_wait_countdown
units.description: Add the growth step and repeat. At the target extent, continue countdown/banner animation until state $11 or later.

units.name: contract_race_window
units.description: Keep the countdown banner updating while reducing the window extent by max(extent/4,1) each frame. Once the next step would underflow, release video inhibition and disable HDMA after synchronized frame waits.

units.name: countdown_track_window_x
units.description: One byte window center per active track0..15; the same track guard used by countdown setup bounds this table.

units.name: countdown_track_window_y
units.description: One byte window center per active track0..15; the same track guard used by countdown setup bounds this table.

units.name: countdown_track_vram_destinations
units.description: Sixteen little-endian VRAM word destinations, one per active track. Countdown rendering indexes by twice the track number.

units.name: draw_track_countdown_frame
units.description:
Select the track-specific destination and a three-byte map source indexed by countdown state. Draw it using a fixed rectangle descriptor.
Decrement the per-state delay; its reload tail advances the selector every six updates.

units.name: advance_track_countdown_frame
units.description: Reload delay to five after underflow and increment the countdown selector; the inclusive countdown therefore lasts six calls per state.

units.name: return_countdown_draw
units.description: Restore status after countdown rendering.

units.name: countdown_rectangle_sources
units.description: 34packed source records: CPU address low/high followed by source bank. The countdown state selects a stride3record; repeated pointers deliberately share tilemaps.

units.name: countdown_rectangle_descriptor
units.description: Rectangle copy descriptor: two control/size words followed by16palette-remap bytes. Its existing consumer combines the paired7-by-7map domain with this descriptor; control bits are retained literally.

units.name: begin_human_race_pause_control
units.description: Preserve status and test the saved controller/pause-owner byte before polling for a new Start owner. Its nonzero branch tests the owning controller release and updates the saved owner state.

units.name: test_pause_owner_release
units.description: Convert the saved owner slot to a controller-word offset and test its Start bit. A held Start follows the shared pause path; release clears the owner/history byte. Static pause mechanics are established, but ordinary gameplay reachability was not observed.

units.name: find_pause_start_in_first_two_trucks
units.description: Test joined bits and Start for the first human truck, then begin the second slot test. Candidate owner IDs are one-based.

units.name: test_player_two_pause_start
units.description: Test player two's automatic controller high byte for Start and join the owner-selection path when pressed.

units.name: test_third_pause_candidate
units.description: Advance the owner ID and test the third joined truck bit. The adjacent branch reads that controller Start bit before owner selection.

units.name: test_player_three_pause_start
units.description: Test player three's automatic controller high byte for Start and join the owner-selection path when pressed.

units.name: test_fourth_pause_candidate
units.description: Advance the owner ID and test the fourth joined truck bit; no joined candidate returns through the separate tail.

units.name: test_shared_pause_start_path
units.description: Retest the third automatic controller word's Start bit; release selects the common continuation. Preserve the encoded $421D access rather than assuming a fourth-controller symmetry.

units.name: save_pause_owner_and_read_controller
units.description: Save the one-based pause owner, run the pause transition helper and read that owner's controller high byte. The adjacent wait loop requires release then a new press; this is statically supported pause logic, with natural use still unobserved.

units.name: wait_pause_release_then_press
units.description: Wait for the owning controller to release Start and press it again. Synchronize the resume transition, release video inhibition and disable HDMA. This loop's intended pause use remains statically inferred.

units.name: return_human_race_control
units.description: Restore status after human race/pause control.

units.name: draw_pause_banner_rectangle
units.description: Use the track's banner VRAM destination plus $41 and draw the pause rectangle from bank $07 source $DAB4. Preserve processor status around the common rectangle helper.

units.name: pause_banner_descriptor
units.description: Twenty-byte count-bounded rectangle descriptor: width/flags word, row-count word and sixteen palette-remap bytes. The pause banner source is CPU $07DAB4; static pause layout does not claim natural reachability.

units.name: wait_pause_transition_frame
units.description: Save status, establish byte accumulator mode and wait a frame before the separately described pause-window expansion.

units.name: expand_pause_window
units.description: Set color math and brightness, select window shape two and draw the pause banner. Increase its extent by eight per frame until $60, then restore the saved status. The caller owns the matching stack/status contract; no runtime pause fetch was observed.

units.name: track_route_pointer_and_stream_bundle
units.description:
32 bank-zero waypoint pointers: sixteen normal and sixteen reversed tracks. Each bounded stream ends at a word with high byte $FF; its low byte sets the checkpoint count.
Coordinate pairs pack half-extents in the low five bits, alongside route-control words. Consumer and inspected terminators establish storage extents. Reverse track 09 remains naturally unobserved.

units.name: upload_audio_block_streams
units.description:
Request SPC reload, then upload two streams rooted at CPU $0E8000 and $0F8000. Each record begins with little-endian length and ARAM destination.
Internal $E028 waits for the IPL $BBAA handshake, sends bytes with an incrementing acknowledgement token and installs each block destination through ports 2/3.
A zero-length record ends transfer and supplies the execution address. Clear all four ports after acknowledgement and restore status. ROM storage and ARAM execution identities remain separate.

units.name: bank_fill_00609c
units.description:
FF allocation fill after upload_audio_blocks, ending at physical $007FC0.
Boundary evidence: Final $00E09B RTS terminates the status-balanced IPL upload helper. Both upload streams are long-indirect sources $0E8000/$0F8000, not this bank-zero tail. Header begins at validated $00FFC0.
The independently bounded predecessor and allocation edge, exact FF homogeneity and repeated bank-tail layout jointly support padding. Bounded reference/source-window checks found no competing established object. This does not identify the historical linker or prove that every possible reader avoids the interval.

units.name: snes_header_and_vectors
units.description:
LoROM cartridge metadata, checksum/complement and native/emulation interrupt vectors. Reset is $8000 and NMI $9BCA in CPU bank zero.
These encoded values are preserved; a faithful rebuild does not repair the original checksum.

units.name: truck_pose_graphics_strips
units.description: Packed truck pose graphics selected by the full supported heading/tilt producer domain. Pose words 0..415 select two 64-byte strips separated by $200 bytes, packed across CPU banks $01/$02. The physical union is $008000..$015000; do not read this as a flat animation-frame array.

units.name: shared_sprites_and_track_asset_union
units.description:
Overlapping immutable source union for shared sprite transfers and track graphics/terrain. Labels below identify independently bounded views without duplicating bytes.
Track graphics DMA requests $8000 bytes; terrain copies read $16B1 bytes into $7F0000. The $02D000 shared-sprite request crosses a DMA bank boundary; only its actual ROM-backed prefix is included by that contract.
Some source spans overlap or share storage, so the region is a physical union rather than a claim of one asset format.

Boundary evidence: Shared sprite palette at CPU $04EB00, physical $026B00: X=0..$FE step2 reads EB00+X and EB01+X, compare $0100. Exact 256-byte end. Separate $02D000 DMA wraps its CPU bank; it does not linearly enter this gap.
The independently bounded predecessor and allocation edge, exact FF homogeneity and repeated bank-tail layout jointly support padding. Bounded reference/source-window checks found no competing established object. This does not identify the historical linker or prove that every possible reader avoids the interval.

units.name: track_terrain_union_04_to_07
units.description:
Union of four track terrain source windows, each read for exactly $16B1 bytes into WRAM $7F0000. Sources overlap physically; internal markers retain each track view.
The runtime sampler uses three-byte terrain cells with neighboring height/control reads; complete artistic/material semantics remain uncertain.

Sixteen-bit sequential VRAM consumer at $00A20D reads $05DAC0+$940.
Storage format follows the transfer contract; individual tile/color content is intentionally left in the local ROM asset.

units.name: spc_upload_block1_header
units.description: Upload record: little-endian length $7E00 and ARAM destination $0400. The main-CPU IPL transfer consumer establishes the exact payload copy and execution handoff; uploaded code is a distinct execution view.

units.name: spc_initialize_and_poll_host
units.description:
Uploaded entry executes at ARAM $0400, stored in the first ROM upload block. Clear direct-page selection, initialize stack and silence DSP master/echo volumes before driver setup.
Poll host flags and commands: command one selects music/state, two requests an effect, three supplies a signed fade step. Host flag $55 mutes/resets DSP and jumps back to IPL for reload.
A changed host heartbeat triggers timer setup, eight-voice processing and a bounded direct-page status dump. Internal $04C7 clears the host command port via CONTROL; $04CE tests effect priority before choosing one of two reserved voice slots.

units.name: spc_start_priority_effect_voice
units.description: Choose reserved voice slot $0C/$0E, clear its DSP noise bit and the listed controls, and install an effect sequence. This is a partial reset: instrument/current pitch persist until prefix/note setup. Supported effects set an instrument before a nonzero interval-zero note; effects5/6 set AC first, but immediate note initialization precedes dependent tick reads. Effect selectors use three complete inferred 16-byte arrays: low/high sequence pointer and priority. No encoded selector bound of 16 is present; descriptor 6 aliases 5. Partial voice reset still requires setup before dependent pitch reads.

units.name: spc_update_master_fade_and_eight_voices
units.description:
Integrate the signed master fade step, clamp its high byte to $00..$7F and stop the step at the limit. An optional host flag divides update frequency by 32.
Commit key-on/noise masks, update eight even-indexed voice records, commit key-off and write each voice's volume/pitch/source registers. Finally set left/right master volume from the fade high byte.
Internal $05FD sends all 256 direct-page bytes to host ports as diagnostics; $060B clears driver state and begins loading sixteen sequence-pointer bytes from parallel song tables.

units.name: spc_load_song_and_process_voice
units.description:
Finish sixteen sequence pointers, select a song parameter block and copy exactly 141 bytes into ARAM $1097..$1124, replacing initial envelope records 1..20 and record21 timer at $1123. Mark eight voices active and assign DSP register bases.
Internal $068A clears direct-page driver state and two overlapping 256-byte voice-state spans; initialize even duration counters to one.
Internal $06AB skips inactive voices, loads a voice mask and decrements note duration. Negative sequence commands dispatch through pushed return addresses; that dispatch table remains structurally unresolved.
Ordinary notes run envelope/modulation/pitch helpers and combine base pitch, signed slide and modulation into the DSP pitch shadow. $06FD begins the pitch-versus-target comparison.

units.name: spc_pitch_envelope_and_modulation_helpers
units.description:
Finish comparing the two-byte current pitch against target; internal $070F snaps current pitch to target.
$071C steps an envelope target on a reloadable timer. $0742 slews the current envelope value toward that target with a bounded step and recalculates pitch.
$0786 applies a delayed alternating signed pitch offset and reverses its direction on period expiry. $07D4 begins the pitch-portamento path, choosing add/subtract toward the target.
Voice records use even X offsets; timers and two-byte fields occupy paired arrays rather than one contiguous structure. The initial envelope image has 28 records of seven fields: tick reload, start level, rise duration, peak level, fall duration, sustain level, release duration. Song configuration mutates $1097..$1124, including record21 timer. Consumers read current ARAM, not immutable ROM defaults.

units.name: spc_portamento_and_sequence_envelopes
units.description:
Move current two-byte pitch toward its target by a per-voice step, snapping at crossings.
Internal $081F clocks an auxiliary parameter stream; negative tokens reset or loop its cursor, ordinary bytes update the envelope target. At a note phase boundary, scan to its next negative terminator.
Internal $085F initializes release/envelope state when the duration reaches its key-off point, then dispatches a stage through pushed return addresses. Those stage targets lie partly in unknown code.

units.name: spc_envelope_dispatch_bytes
units.description: Five low address bytes followed by five high address bytes for the envelope-stage dispatcher. Its bounded stage selector combines corresponding bytes into an ARAM code address; these are split arrays rather than adjacent words.

units.name: interpolate_spc_envelope_stages
units.description: Interpolate successive envelope segments from the $1091 record fields using elapsed ticks and MUL/DIV. Preserve voice indices across arithmetic; zero-duration or exhausted stages take balanced stack exits, advance the envelope stage and reset its tick cursor. The middle entry computes the descending segment toward the next endpoint.

units.name: finish_spc_envelope_release
units.description: Provide the balanced stack-exit tails and release-stage interpolation. Scale the saved envelope amplitude by remaining ticks over duration, write the voice's modulation amplitude and advance the stage when it reaches zero. The isolated earlier RET at ROM $0704FF remains unclassified.

units.name: spc_start_note_and_initialize_voice_effects
units.description:
Continue the note-start path: add instrument/voice offsets to the note value, set envelope target/current values and calculate the target pitch from split tables and an instrument scale.
Initialize modulation delay/direction, envelope phase and duration; combine voice masks into pending key-on/key-off state unless suppressed.
Internal helpers $0984,$09AD,$09C7,$09DC,$09F0 perform pitch scaling, modulation reset, release-threshold selection, envelope-stage reset and next-duration loading. $0A05 reads the next sequence byte through an indexed pointer. Instrument arrays each allocate 32 bytes. Instrument 33 therefore reads note base from scale byte $50A5 and scale from silence byte $50C5; equal effective reads do not create extra array records. Full pitch-table bounds remain unresolved.

units.name: spc_sequence_command_handlers
units.description: Command-specific entries update voice state or redirect sequence flow, then return to the sequence parser. Two-byte targets are little-endian; calls push the current sequence pointer on the per-voice stack, counted loops rewind it until exhausted, and return pops it. Other entries set duration, volume, instrument, auxiliary sequence, pitch/envelope parameters, noise masks and DSP flags. See the internal handler labels for each operand contract; these are uploaded SPC code, not main-CPU ROM execution. Command $8E enters at $0ABB and forces one duration read without an operand. Command $BA enters at $0BE0, clears enable/primary mode and sets secondary mode; it installs no stream pointer. B6 only sets enable to $FF; B8 clears enable/secondary and sets primary.

units.name: spc_command_set_target_envelope

units.name: spc_command_set_auxiliary_stream
units.description: Command98 reads delay and split ARAM pointer, enables auxiliary mode and resumes sequence parsing. Two bounded attack/release streams have independently selected operands; updater distinguishes restart80 from negative hold markers.

units.name: spc_read_auxiliary_stream_byte
units.description: Copy the per-voice auxiliary pointer to scratch, read at its byte cursor and increment that cursor. Return the stream byte; cursor wrapping follows byte arithmetic.

units.name: spc_sequence_stack_helpers
units.description: Pop a two-byte sequence return pointer from the per-voice stack, push one byte, or push the current two-byte sequence pointer. $50+X is the stack cursor into the $0380 workspace; callers establish each stack balance.

units.name: spc_write_voice_dsp_and_initialize_timer

Write six DSP registers for one voice from parallel left/right volume, pitch and source-related shadows; leave unused register slots untouched. Advance the shadow index by two.
Internal $0C8C resets CONTROL, sets timer-zero divisor $42 and enables it. Internal $0C9A writes paired DSP initialization tables until the register list has a negative terminator.
The uploaded lifetime and ROM source association come from the main-CPU upload evidence; equal ARAM bytes alone were not used as provenance.
